data.title: pi-cards: card execution — cards_work tool + /cards work [--todo] (P3)

fields.description:
pi-cards series 6/8 — card execution: cards_work tool + /cards work [--todo] (P3). Spec §6.5, §6.7. Blocked by card 5 (board UI).

Board UI and full tool surface exist; this delivers G4: a subagent executes one card end-to-end with claim CAS, card-focused prompt assembly, and honest close-out (worklog entry, summary comment, transition) — plus sequential batch draining of the todo lane.

Scope:
- `src/work.ts`: `runCard(id, opts)` implementing the §6.5 flow — preflight (`cards_get`; refuse if owned by another actor or terminal status, unless `--force`), claim as resolved actor + status→in_progress when the board declares that transition, prompt assembly (title, type, description, acceptance criteria, comments, one-hop link titles), subagent spawn isolated behind one `spawnSubagent(prompt, cwd, onUpdate)` function (spec open question #3), close-out.
- `cards_work` tool + `/cards work <id>` command sharing `runCard`; board UI `w` key now calls it.
- Close-out: if the card type declares a `work_log` repeating field, append `{author, notes, commit_hash?, timestamp}`; completion comment with `git diff --stat` since claim; success → board's review transition (never auto-`done` unless `work.autoDone:true` and acceptance checkable+passing); failure → leave status, comment failure, release claim unless `--keep`.
- Batch: `/cards work --todo` loops `cards_take_next(status=todo, …)`, sequential, one actor per run, stops at `work.batchLimit` (default 3) or first hard failure; tui mode shows confirm dialog with candidate list; print mode requires `--yes`.
- Handoff comment on the next unstarted card when a batch stops early (§6.7, one comment per batch).

Implementation notes (spawn mechanism verified against pi 0.80.10 `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts`):
- Spawn a separate pi process: `spawn(piInvocation, ["--mode","json","-p","--no-session", "Task: …"], {cwd, stdio:["ignore","pipe","pipe"]})`; resolve the invocation by re-exec'ing `process.argv[1]` with `process.execPath`, falling back to `pi` on PATH.
- Parse stdout line-by-line as JSON events: `message_end` accumulates messages/usage; final output = last assistant text part; stream partials to `onUpdate` and `ctx.ui.setStatus("cards", "working #<short>…")`. Abort: SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 5s.
- Tool inheritance: globally-installed extensions DO load in print mode, so once pi-cards is installed the subagent inherits `cards_*` tools automatically. In dev (`-e` loading), pass `-e <abs path to this extension's index.ts>` explicitly. Project-local `.pi/extensions` will NOT load in the child without a saved trust decision — do not rely on it.
- Record `git rev-parse HEAD` at claim for diff-stat and `commit_hash` resolution at close-out.
- Lost claim race in batch = skip to next candidate, never error.

Acceptance:
- Against a scratch copy of the fixture workspace: `pi -e ./src/index.ts -p "/cards work <id-of-a-todo-card>"` completes — card owner = resolved actor, status `review`, one `work_log` entry with real commit hash, one completion comment with diff stat (verify via `cards get <id>`).
- Failure path: force a failing card → status unchanged, failure comment present, claim released.
- Preflight refuses a card owned by someone else without `--force`, printing current state.
- `/cards work --todo --yes` in print mode processes ≤3 cards sequentially and comments on the next unstarted card.
- `node --test` (prompt assembly, preflight guards, close-out decision matrix with a fake spawn) + typecheck green.

Out of scope: built-in pi `Agent` tool as spawn mechanism (isolated behind `spawnSubagent`); interim per-turn worklogs (card 7); parallel/multi-card concurrency.
- work_log timestamps: compute at close-out with `new Date().toISOString()` (UTC) — never hand-format or stamp local time with a `Z` suffix (loop session 2026-07-18 had to patch-entry four entries for exactly this).

work_log.author: pi
work_log.notes: Execution complete on feat/cards-work: subagent.ts (JSONL spawn per pi 0.80.10 example), work.ts (pure decisions + runCard + runBatch), work-register.ts (cards_work tool + /cards work + board w key). 57/57 tests green. LIVE acceptance on scratch server :8799: trivial card ran end-to-end (claim foz → real subagent → review; worklog w/ full git hash + real UTC; diff-stat comment); preflight refused other-owned card. Learnings: (1) subagent did its own card bookkeeping (duplicate worklog/comment + hallucinated date) — buildPrompt now forbids card mutations + invented timestamps; (2) batch live-run claimed heavy real card 03c836c3, killed by harness timeout — batch mechanics pinned by unit tests instead; (3) release-only-on-HTTP matters for failure close-out in CLI mode (documented in runCard).

comments.body: DONE (pi). feat/cards-work @ 3296ef8, 57/57 tests + tsc green. Acceptance: single-card live run ✓ (scratch :8799 — claim, real subagent, review transition, worklog UTC+hash, diff-stat comment); preflight refusal ✓ live; failure close-out + batch mechanics ✓ unit-tested (fake spawn); live batch attempt claimed a heavy real card and hit the harness timeout (test-data artifact, not a defect). Prompt hardening after the live run: subagent is now forbidden from card bookkeeping (it duplicated worklog/comment and invented a date). Board w key + /cards work --todo [--limit] [--yes] wired.

data.title: CLI: patch/claim without a preceding GET (--if-match latest or auto-retry)

fields.acceptance: 1) `cards patch <id> --status done --if-match latest` succeeds with no prior GET (server re-reads current version under the write lock). 2) A concurrent-writer test pins who wins when two `--if-match latest` writes race: the second returns 409 version_conflict, exit code 4. 3) Explicit `--version N` guard is unchanged: a stale version still returns 409, exit code 4. 4) `cards claim` gains the same `--if-match latest` affordance. 5) Default behavior (no flag, no version) is unchanged for `patch`/`claim` — still errors with the existing 'usage' message, so the safe default is preserved.
fields.description:
Problem: `cards patch` and `cards claim` REQUIRE `--version` (commands.go:168, :239), so every scripted mutation must do a GET first to fetch the current version. That is friction for agents and one-shot shell scripts.

Add an opt-in convenience that stays safe by default: `--if-match latest`, where the server re-reads the card's current version under the write lock and applies the mutation in one round-trip. This is preferred over a client-side fetch+retry-on-409 loop because it closes the race server-side (the read and the conditional write share one lock). Document the race semantics honestly: two concurrent `--if-match latest` writes still conflict — the second sees the version bumped by the first and returns 409 (exit code 4), exactly like an explicit stale `--version`.

The explicit `--version N` guard remains the canonical optimistic-concurrency path and is unchanged. `--if-match latest` is purely a convenience for the no-prior-GET case.

Out of scope: changing the default (no-flag) behavior, multi-write transactions, or any change to the HTTP `If-Match`/version contract.
fields.verify: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestPatchIfMatchLatest and TestClaimIfMatchLatest; add a concurrent-writer test asserting the loser gets exit code 4.

comments.author: foz
comments.body:
**Review (batch C, keep backlog).**

**Validated:** `--version` is required for both `patch` (commands.go:168) and `claim` (commands.go:239); 409 maps to exit code 4 (cli_test.go:47, client.go:199 `ExitCode`). No `--if-match`/auto-retry path exists today. Claims accurate.

**Issues found:** Original acceptance bundled "concurrent-writer test pins who wins" without stating the expected loser behavior (exit 4). Did not explicitly state the default (no-flag) path is preserved — important for the "safe by default" claim.

**Changes made:** Rewrote description as problem → solution → race semantics → out-of-scope. Added 5 numbered acceptance checks (incl. default-path preserved and `claim` parity). Replaced verify with named test fns for both patch and claim plus the concurrent-loser test. api_change confirmed additive.

**Scope verdict:** Tight and correctly bounded — one opt-in flag, no contract change. Keep backlog.

**Arch verdict:** Aligned. Server-side re-read under the write lock is the right call (closes the race rather than papering over it with client retry), and preserving the explicit `--version` guard keeps the optimistic-concurrency contract intact.

data.title: Bug: stale-version modal save toasts 'Saved' while dropping the write

fields.description:
Found during rebuild Phase 2 verification (pre-existing, NOT a rebuild regression — reproduced identically on the pre-rebuild code path).

REPRO: POST /ui/cards/{id}/save with a stale version and a changed title → HTTP 200, write correctly rejected by CAS server-side, BUT: uiSaveCard's error branch re-renders the modal WITH the error attached at HTTP 200 (internal/httpapi/ui.go, PatchCard err branch). Client wireDirtySave checks r.ok → sees 200 → toasts 'Saved' and swaps in the error-bearing modal. User sees a green 'Saved' toast while their change was dropped (the embedded error alert renders, but the toast contradicts it).

FIX (belongs to rebuild Phase 4's shared cardsAPI.send() helper — version-aware fetch + structured-error parse in ONE place): either (a) server returns the real 4xx status with the re-rendered modal body (client swaps on !ok too, shows error toast via apiErrText), or (b) client inspects the swapped HTML for the error alert before toasting. (a) is honest HTTP and matches the /v1 transports' contract (fail loudly, guide recovery).

Acceptance: stale-version save shows a version-conflict toast + the modal error (no 'Saved'); fresh save still toasts 'Saved'; detail-page save path same contract; regression test on the save handler status code.

data.title: UI: harden $store.live reconnect (single socket, generation guard)

fields.a11y: If live status is exposed, keep non-color text/status for reconnecting/down (optional UI).
fields.acceptance: Never more than one EventSource to /v1/events/stream per tab; reconnect resumes with since=lastId; no silent total death of live updates without user-visible hint after sustained failure.
fields.description:
Sprint 07-10 P4 must-ship #4 (tracker card_3f225267). Follow-on to P9 filter-stall fix and closed card 60f2e6a8. DEPENDS ON: thin harness card_0391870a (the gen-guard invariant needs a Node unit test to live in).

Risks still present:
- onerror schedules open() with overlapping timers if errors cluster
- no generation token: stale EventSource handlers can deliver after replace
- live handler exceptions swallowed (empty catch) — swapBoard failures go silent
- handlers array not idempotent across remounts if stop() not paired

FIX:
1) WRITTEN CONTRACT first: code comment above $store.live specifying exactly what open()/stop()/onerror/onmessage do w.r.t. the generation counter — stop() closes the ES, bumps the generation, clears pending delivery (not just a token check in onerror). Do NOT change on/off signatures.
2) reconnectTimer cleared on stop/open; generation++ per open; ignore mismatched es.
3) assert single es; close previous before assign.
4) log/count handler errors; toast after N consecutive swap failures.
5) Decision logic in a pure shouldDeliver(gen, currentGen)-style helper, unit-tested in the Node harness.

OUT OF SCOPE: extending TestSSEKeepalive — a server-side test cannot pin a client-side invariant; the server test guarantees keepalive only.

VERIFY: DevTools — one EventSource across 20 filter toggles; kill server briefly; one reconnect backoff; no duplicate board thrash. DUAL-CONSUMER check recorded here: board tab + /ui/breaches tab, server kill-and-restart, each event delivers once, no stale ES delivers after stop().

ACC: never more than one EventSource to /v1/events/stream per tab; reconnect resumes with since=lastId; Node test pins the generation invariant; no silent death of live updates without a user-visible hint after sustained failure.

FOLDED IN from the PR #18 Copilot review (2026-07-10) — two latent handler-lifecycle bugs, benign today because boardPage lives on the persistent .board-view root (init runs once), but exactly the reconnect/remount hazards this card exists to close:
- $store.live on() is NOT idempotent: start() has a same-boardId/types guard, but on() always pushes a new closure. A re-init (parent initTree, or a future SPA nav path) would stack duplicate debouncedSwap calls per SSE event. FIX with the generation guard: clear/replace handlers on (re)start, or key delivery by generation so stale closures no-op.
- boardPage.init() adds a window popstate listener with no teardown. Same persistent-root reason it is harmless now; add removal via Alpine $destroy/destroy() so it cannot stack if navigation ever goes through a fragment path.
Both should be covered by the written open/stop/onerror/onmessage + handler-lifecycle contract this card already calls for.

links.note: gen-guard unit test needs the Node harness

comments.author: claude
comments.body: Done + committed to main. $store.live hardened with a generation counter (bumped on open/stop; superseded ES self-silence via shouldDeliver), tracked reconnectTimer, idempotent on()/off(), and destroy() cleanup on boardPage+breachesPage (fixes the two #18-review findings: on() dedup + popstate cleanup). Also fixed a pre-existing backoff bug — resetting backoff in open() defeated the ramp; moved to es.onopen so it truly ramps 500ms→8s (verified: ~4 attempts over 6s down, was ~35). data.title: Review minors batch: watch/reload startup races + suppression window; date min/max author UX; conflict-shape consistency

fields.description:
Batch of small correctness/polish items from the sprint 07-11 post-merge review (b23aff8) — reload/watch startup + config authoring UX. Each is a contained fix; land as one branch of small commits.

RELOAD/WATCH (flagged independently by two reviewers):
1) setAfterReload ordering race: cmd/cards/serve.go:126 starts the watcher before setAfterReload at :160; plain field write (reload.go:81-83) read by notifyReload — no happens-before. Failure: missed service reconcile on a first-tick reload under --watch --run-extensions. FIX: install before spawning the watcher (one-line move) or make the field atomic.
2) Watcher not awaited on shutdown: watchCancel deferred but Run not joined (contrast supervisor's supDone, serve.go:163-173); SIGINT during scanOnce can race reloadLocked against store close. FIX: done channel like the supervisor's.
3) Self-write suppression window swallows a concurrent external edit: while selfWriteGate.active>0, scanOnce absorbs ANY fingerprint and advances lastFP (watch.go:114-118) — an external save during the create-board handler window is silently dropped until the next change. FIX: during active window skip WITHOUT advancing lastFP; only skipFP should advance it.
4) Stale skipFP can absorb a later legitimate change (watch.go:207-211): cleared only on match; if the first post-create observation differs, it lingers and can swallow an exact-revert later. FIX: one-tick TTL.
5) Timing-sensitive negatives noted by review: TestSupervisorUsesCurrentGenerationAfterSwap proves the negative with a fixed 500ms sleep; TestWatchSelfWriteSuppressed drains fan-out non-blockingly. No observed flake in 25x -race; tighten opportunistically.

CONFIG AUTHORING UX:
6) FieldDate min/max units undocumented + hostile errors: values are Unix-seconds floats sharing the number slots (core/types.go:47-48); no author-facing doc; '"min": "2020-01-01"' yields a raw json.Unmarshal error and runtime rejection prints 'below min 1.5778368e+09' — fails the project's own which-field/which-value/what-was-allowed bar. FIX: document units in DEVELOPER-REFERENCE-SCHEMA-AUTHORING.md; render dates as RFC3339 in the error; consider accepting date strings at load.
7) Store-level version_conflict returns the ATTEMPTED card, not current DB state (internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:587-588) — matters for the versionless MCP tools under a genuine race. Pre-existing; fix while nearby.
8) RemoveEntry rejects version 0 as validation error while AppendEntry/UpdateEntry treat omitted version as version_conflict — inconsistent shape; pick one.

VERIFY: go test -race ./cmd/cards ./internal/hooks ./internal/sqlite; go vet.

data.title: Sprint 07-22 P5: schema-authoring UI — create-first, additive-safe (one schema, every transport)

fields.description:
Sprint 07-22 Phase 5 of docs/plans/2026-07-22-sprint-plan.md — make "one schema drives every transport" tangible: author card-type schemas from the web UI. Internally ordered create-first so a mid-phase cut still ships the core slice (create-a-new-type lands before any edit capability).

## Context
Depends on Phase 1 (writeDefinitionAndReload helper — the diff check lives there) and Phase 2 (affected-card counts in rejection copy come from the query endpoint). The mutability invariant is framed on the EXISTING versioning model — cards carry schema_version; Service.UpgradeSchema (internal/core/service.go:937) re-pins one card at a time, forward-only — NOT a parallel invented migration concept.

## DO (contract before form code — hard ordering)
1. **Write the versioning/mutability contract in docs/reference/card-definitions.md FIRST**: (a) creating a type starts at schema_version 1; (b) an additive edit — new OPTIONAL field WITH a default; no removal, no narrowing, no required-without-default — bumps schema_version; (c) existing cards stay pinned at their old version, the new field is documented as absent until re-pinned via UpgradeSchema on next explicit touch; mixed-version reads are a documented, VALID state. The general migration engine is honestly deferred with the seam named.
2. **Card-type write path on the Phase-1 helper**: POST (create) and PATCH (additive edit) validate → diff-check → write → reload atomically on the shared mutex semantics. The old-vs-new additive-only diff check lives in writeDefinitionAndReload — NOT in validateCardType, which validates a single CardType in isolation and also runs at cold startup, so a diff rule there would wrongly reject hand-edited definitions/ files on boot. validateCardType stays a pure single-def validator (it does gain the unconditional "new-in-def optional fields must carry defaults" rules that hold for any single def). Unsafe edits rejected with a structured error naming the offending field and why; contract test pins the shapes.
3. **Authoring form** (server-rendered templates + Alpine.js, board_create.html pattern, role-token contract — see docs/architecture/design-system.md) covering the 10 field types and their extra keys (options, item_fields, artifact_policy, option_themes with the 4.5:1 contrast floor) — WITH the UX that makes it usable: additive-only rejections surface as human-readable in-form messages tied to the offending field, including the reason and the affected-card count (queried via POST /v1/cards/query); empty state; inline validation; WYSIWYG edit-geometry conformance. No new build step.
4. **MCP drift signal, minimal honest shape**: stdio MCP has no server-push channel, so a live-session handshake is impossible — instead echo the workspace schema_version in every tool result so a client detects drift on its next call; document agent-facing behavior (on mismatch: re-introspect or reconnect; in-flight writes remain valid BECAUSE edits are additive-optional-default — that invariant is enforced by the diff check, not an accident). If the echo proves invasive mid-phase, fall back to docs-only and say so on this card.

## Demo
Create a brand-new card type in the web UI and immediately create a card of it — one authored schema drives the web form, CLI, API response, and regenerated OpenAPI. Then make an additive edit and show BOTH sides of the invariant: an existing card reads back valid at its old schema_version, and an unsafe edit is rejected with copy a human understands.

## Expected outcomes / exit
- Versioning contract in card-definitions.md lands before any form code; mixed-version reads documented as valid.
- Additive-only diff check enforced in writeDefinitionAndReload (loader untouched); unsafe edits → structured errors; contract test green.
- Form covers all 10 field types incl. contrast floor, in-form rejection copy with affected-card counts, WYSIWYG geometry; go test ./internal/httpapi passes (template parse).
- schema_version echoed in MCP tool results with documented recovery, or the docs-only fallback recorded here with reasoning.

data.title: Core/HTTP: card delete (DELETE /v1/cards/:id + tombstone event + idempotency)

fields.description:
Add a first-class card-delete path so junk/test/superseded cards can be hard-removed instead of being closed-as-done with a comment (the current workaround used during the 2026-07 board cleanup, which hit exactly this gap).

Scope:
- DELETE /v1/cards/:id HTTP route (mirror existing PATCH auth/actor/idempotency: X-Work-Cards-Actor header, Idempotency-Key, optimistic version in ?version= query param).
- CLI: `cards delete <id> --version N` (serverless + HTTP, like patch/claim).
- MCP: a `delete_card` tool (the MCP tool list currently has no delete either).
- Core: Service.RemoveCard(id, version, actor) — atomic. Emit a new `card_removed` durable event (typed constructor in internal/core/events.go per EVENTS.md §4 no-raw-literals rule) carrying the removed card's id/type/title snapshot in Diff for replay/audit. Persist via the existing commitCard seam (or the ClaimAtomic-style atomic path if no card row update is needed — decide and document).
- Safety: delete is a hard, irreversible mutation. Require the current version (optimistic concurrency) so a stale client cannot delete a card that changed underneath it. Consider a workspace setting to soft-delete (tombstone) vs hard-delete; default to hard-delete + event to match append-only audit design. Refusing to delete a card that still has inbound links is an open question — propose: reject with 409 if any inbound links exist (caller removes links first), OR cascade-remove the card's links but refuse to cascade across cards. Pick one and document in SPEC.md §11.
- Docs: SPEC.md §11 (add the route), §8 (add card_removed to the event catalog + diff shape), INTEGRATOR-REFERENCE.md §2/§4, MCP.md (tool table), DEVELOPER-REFERENCE.md §9 (CLI). Status: [proposed].

Out of scope: bulk delete, undo/recycle, retention windows.

Acceptance:
- `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` green with new tests covering: delete by current version succeeds and emits card_removed; stale version returns 409 version_conflict; delete is idempotent under a replayed Idempotency-Key (returns the original 204/200); deleting a card with inbound links behaves per the chosen policy with a test.
- OpenAPI spec (internal/openapi) updated; `cards delete` works in both serverless and HTTP modes; MCP `delete_card` tool listed and working.

data.title: Sprint 2026-07-11: make the composition substrate real (tracker)

fields.description:
SPRINT TRACKER — plan doc: docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-11.md. The board IS the plan: card bodies carry the executable detail; phase exits update statuses on the card IDs below.

PITCH: Rotate the center of mass back onto the differentiating substrate — the four transports as honest versioned contracts, and the extensions-over-plugins bet. Drain review + retire doc drift first (P0, hard gate), make MCP a first-class transport + raise config validation rigor (P2), then in PARALLEL: live definition authoring with in-browser failure feedback (P3) and enum-driven board legibility (P4), finishing with the north star: a supervised 'service' extension kind (P5). Every schema change this sprint is additive omitempty definition JSON — no SQLite migration, no snapshot-format change.

PHASES → CARDS:
P0a card_9174c0ea607a40ef8ebe6cb3b75f2932 (review-pile drain, per-card verify)
P0b card_bac182247e6144f7942c8058787e5619 (doc-truth sync: INTEGRATOR-REFERENCE / SPEC-API-SURFACE / mcp README)
P2a card_c3c0fac556144a54a3be69d012e93b75 (six MCP tools + parity allowlist test)
P2b card_8b25cef932d84aa7b90ede8a5921e946 (config semantic validation, warn-tier)
P3a card_524c5758b3b34e4d814142130cab9eca (hook-supervisor stale-generation bug — cherry-picks forward)
P3b card_ec61b093d1a444dcb5c915518de5c67f (--watch poller + failure banner + reload contract)
P4a card_1af1fd87334f4e078b02e0ab14649446 (golden-render harness + TypeTheme unification)
P4b card_4bdd35866cc54e4e844b5f6d96da6a8e (style_field: color+icon per enum value)
P5a card_abb13ae015a843f4b00b52a65b81fc1c (lifecycle ADR: RestartPolicy x Autostart x kinds)
P5b card_23c7070a75114ba9ad14306803293f4f (service supervisor: ready gate, backoff, drain)
P5c card_eecf0e0303a24b328b9993d547c4df65 (reconcile-on-reload: identity key + decision table)
CLOSE card_c08a6ead73a04837995484a5ba9177d7 (walkthrough + round-trip + board sync)
CARRY-OVER card_f20e87d5da85410cbcf18b4ccda9dd5a (board-create idempotency — unfinished 07-10 work; finish narrowly or close-blocker)

STANDING RULES: P0 gates all M-sized work. No batch-flipping review cards — human git show / CI verification per card. Every schema change stays additive omitempty definition JSON. Phase exits update card statuses. Sprint close exports + commits the JSONL once.

OUT OF SCOPE (deliberate): click-accent-to-filter (follow-up card against shipped style_field) · token-mode auth (AUTH.md frozen; host-shaped until multi-tenant is scheduled) · ACL/permissions in kernel · expose field semantics · outbox/webhooks in-core (future home: an external supervised service) · hook re-declaration on reload (rides P5 reconcile design or follow-up) · DisallowUnknownFields (key leniency is what keeps this sprint's schema changes safe) · orphaned View type · GH-Pages docs site · enum theming beyond one style_field per board · fsnotify.

RISKS: stricter validation is a load-contract change — warn-tier is the pressure valve; validate demo-workspace + known definitions before any rejection ships. Stale-generation bug is live and watcher-amplified — P3a cherry-picks forward even if P3 slips. Watcher + supervisor tests are the flake-prone surfaces — injectable clock / fake child binaries / mac+linux budget are designed in. P5 has the most unknowns at the end of the critical path — ADR lands early; fallback is supervisor-without-reconcile (documented restart-on-reload). Golden harness fallback: snapshot only type-themed demo boards. Pipeline is review-bound: P0 is a hard gate and per-card verification keeps it honest.

data.title: Sprint 07-11 P5b: supervise kind:service — listener-ready gate, crash-loop backoff with min-healthy-uptime, bounded drain

fields.description:
Phase 5 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-11.md. Audience: the extension developer — judged on 'an external process I wrote in any language survives crashes and consumes events'. Turns extensions-over-plugins into working mechanism.

DO — the supervised-process class with real lifecycle semantics:
1) Listener-ready gate: start services only after the net.Listener is accepting (create the listener before the supervisor goroutine, or pass a readiness channel); hand each child the loopback base URL via env so 'how does the service find the server' is defined, not assumed.
2) Bounded backoff WITH a minimum-healthy-uptime threshold before the counter resets — a runs-briefly-then-crashes service escalates to the cap instead of pinning CPU. Crash-loop test REQUIRED.
3) Bounded drain: SIGTERM, configurable grace period, then SIGKILL the process group (reuse hooks.go's procgroup fallback). A SIGTERM-ignoring child must be force-killed within the grace window — test REQUIRED. Shutdown always returns.
4) ONE shared supervisor-construction path used by both serve --run-extensions (serve.go:130) and standalone run-extensions (extensions.go:56); the ADR names serve --run-extensions as the supported home.

Budget explicitly for mac+linux race-clean signal tests (fake crashing/hanging child binaries) — the existing procgroup_unix/other split shows this does not come free.

FALLBACK if P2/P3 slip badly: ship supervisor-without-reconcile (services restart on every reload, documented) rather than slipping the whole north star.

ACCEPTANCE: kind:service autostarts after the listener accepts; restarts per policy without crash-loop CPU pinning; hung child force-killed within grace; both entry points share one wiring; go test ./... green and race-clean on mac+linux.

data.title: Harden store error mapping: GetCard/ClaimAtomic swallow DB errors as 404/empty

fields.description: Two fail-soft paths mask infrastructure failures. (1) Service.GetCard maps ANY store error to NotFound(404), so a DB outage looks like 'card not found'. data.title: Events seam 3d: deadline min-heap scheduler for temporal conditions (status_timeout, card_idle)

fields.description: docs/EVENTS.md §11.2; design already refined in INTEGRATION.md comments (deadline min-heap, no fixed tick, sleeps until earliest deadline, empty heap = no wakeups). This is the hardest and riskiest piece of the condition-event system — land it as its own isolated slice, after the instant-condition machinery (3a-3c) has already validated Signal/Emit/persist:true. Deadlines armed from a denormalized status_since column + a fired-marker keyed by (card,status,status_since); reconstructible from state, nothing persisted for scheduling itself. Lazy/refcounted: only scheduled while a monitor has a live consumer (SSE filter, hook/webhook, or persist:true), dropped when the last consumer disconnects. Acceptance: unit-testable scheduler with an injected clock (no real sleeps in tests); zero-wakeup idle test (empty heap does not spin); refcount test (deadline dropped when last consumer disconnects, re-armed on reconnect); crossing-state idempotency test.

links.note: builds on the validated condition-event plumbing

comments.author: jeremy
comments.body: Plan refined (EVENTS.md §12 Step 3d, PR #16). Confirmed shape: min-heap, no fixed tick, sleep-until-earliest, empty heap = zero wakeups; deadlines reconstructible from status_since + fired-marker keyed by (card,status,status_since). Adjustment: the scheduler emits via Condition (3b) so it holds NO durability opinion — this is why 3b lands before 3d. Note the edge: a persist:true temporal type is a PERMANENT consumer, so its deadline never refcounts to zero ('lazy' doesn't apply to it — call it out).

data.title: Snapshot merge driver: semantic git merge for backlog.jsonl

fields.description:
A `cards merge-snapshot` command registered as a git merge driver (.gitattributes) for backlog.jsonl. Makes the git-synced team topology safe instead of 'avoid concurrent edits to the same card' (docs/using-cards.md 'Conflicts').

SAFE-BY-CONSTRUCTION SETS: comments (cm_ ids — internal/core/helpers.go:23) and repeating-field entries (entry_id — internal/core/service.go:~1057) are append-only; union by id is always safe and never conflicts.

ENVELOPE/FIELDS: three-way merge; highest version wins where unambiguous (the snapshot already sorts one card per line in stable order, so different-card edits already auto-merge — this handles same-card divergence). Both-sides-moved-status (or any genuinely ambiguous field change) punts to manual with a clear, structured message naming the card, the field, and both candidate values.

SCOPE: the merge-snapshot subcommand + .gitattributes registration + docs. Reads base/ours/theirs from git's %O %A %B tokens.

OUT OF SCOPE: semantic merge of arbitrary field-value conflicts beyond highest-version-wins; merging across divergent schema versions; auto-resolving status moves.

DONE WHEN: cards merge-snapshot is registered as the backlog.jsonl git merge driver; a reproducible same-card-divergence scenario (two commenters, or a field change + a comment) merges cleanly via id-union; a both-sides-moved-status conflict leaves a clean conflict marker and a message naming the card; docs/using-cards.md 'Conflicts' references the driver.

VERIFY: construct backlog.jsonl divergence (same card, disjoint comments + one field bump); run cards merge-snapshot; assert clean id-union; construct a status-move conflict; assert manual punt with a clear message naming the card.

comments.author: foz
comments.body:
**Quality review (batch A)**

**Validated**
- Comments use `cm_` ids (`internal/core/helpers.go:23`) and repeating entries use `entry_id` (`internal/core/service.go:~1057`) — both are stable, server-generated, append-only. "Union by id is always safe" is correct.
- Snapshot is sorted one-card-per-line in stable order (`docs/using-cards.md` 'Conflicts'), so different-card edits already auto-merge and this driver only needs to handle same-card divergence — accurately scoped.
- No `merge-snapshot` command exists today — genuine gap.

**Issues found**
- No done-when / observable verify.
- "Both-sides-moved-status punts to manual" was stated but without specifying the message shape (which card, which field, both values).

**Changes made**
- Pinned the code refs for `cm_` and `entry_id`.
- Specified the manual-punt message shape: name the card, the field, and both candidate values (philosophy §9 — fail loudly, guide recovery).
- Added SCOPE (git %O %A %B tokens) / OUT OF SCOPE (no semantic field-conflict resolution, no cross-schema-version merge, no auto status resolution) / DONE WHEN / VERIFY.
- Added a concrete verify scenario: same-card divergence with disjoint comments + a field bump merges cleanly; a status-move conflict punts manually with a clear message.

**Scope verdict**: keep-as-is — one subcommand + driver registration; correctly narrow.
**Arch verdict**: aligned — union-by-id leverages existing stable ids (schemas, not magic), highest-version-wins is transparent, and manual punt with a structured message matches philosophy §9.

data.title: AUTH reference impl: register issues bearer token; --auth token verifies writes

fields.acceptance: Tests: happy path (200 with valid bearer); 401 on missing/invalid/unknown token (identical generic body — no enumeration); constant-time compare unit test; CRITICAL anti-spoof test: valid bearer + mismatched X-Work-Cards-Actor commits with the AUTHENTICATED actor (assert on the event's actor field); forced write without credentials → 401; --auth none regression: existing httpapi tests pass unchanged; identity-before-idempotency: same Idempotency-Key under two different tokens creates two distinct writes. SPEC-API-SURFACE gains 'Security / Actor' subsection ONLY when this lands; PHILOSOPHY §1/§7 edits land in the same commit train.
fields.description:
Reference implementation of docs/design/AUTH.md (frozen 2026-07-10 — the doc is normative for this card; see docs/NOTES.md freeze entry). AUTH.md review has landed (card_61040a3e, done 2026-07-18); the doc is frozen and normative. This card remains parked in backlog until an owner schedules the XL sprint — reopening the design requires impl-discovers-reality, not another investigation pass.

BEHAVIOR (AUTH.md §§1-4):
- cards serve --auth <none|token> (proxy mode is a LATER slice, not this card).
- POST /v1/users issues an opaque high-entropy bearer token, shown once. DB stores hash only (constant-time compare via crypto/subtle). No GET-token endpoint. Rotate = revoke + reissue (cards users token rotate <id>).
- Writes under --auth token require Authorization: Bearer; actor = the registered User.ID the token maps to. Reads stay open in v0 (host ACL is the read confidentiality line; --auth-require-read is future work).
- Under --auth none: today's behavior exactly — ambient hints (X-Work-Cards-Actor → CARDS_USER → DefaultUser), actor may be an unregistered free string, Kind best-effort. DefaultUser is NOT consulted under token.
- Bootstrap: serverless CLI register always trusted; HTTP POST /v1/users under token gated by an existing valid bearer (v0 stopgap: first CLI-registered user is the admin bit — see card_2680d5f7 for the debt). --save writes ~/.cards/credentials; CARDS_TOKEN env supported (MCP adapter binds identity at process spawn).
- Identity resolves BEFORE idempotency replay (AUTH.md §5 — keys are per-actor).
- 401 for ALL failure modes; no user enumeration; rate-silenced failure logs; NEVER log token material.
- Force never bypasses auth: forced writes still 401 without valid credentials.

NOT THIS CARD: proxy mode, --auth-require-read, sessions/cookies (reference-client pattern — the web UI may store the bearer client-side; that is a separate thin follow-on spike), Basic-auth adapter (optional later: Basic maps user:token onto the same store — one-line mention in AUTH.md §11, do NOT implement in v0), scoped tokens, groups semantics.

DOWNSTREAM: landing this unblocks card_c7a70b64 Child C (wire Service.ResolveActor as the Authenticator default fallback).

BIND WARN INTERACTION: pairs with card_fa239a92 — non-loopback + auth=none gets the extra remediation line; non-loopback + auth=token gets the single WARN only.
fields.endpoint: HTTP auth middleware on /v1/* and /ui/* writes (no new route)
fields.verify: go test ./internal/httpapi ./cmd/cards; curl -u flow per acceptance; cards users register --save then cards create without --as → event actor = registered id

data.title: Sprint 07-22 P2: POST /v1/cards/query — decided contract + endpoint (early user win)

fields.acceptance: Contract documented in query-dsl.md + api-surface.md (incl. the declined GET ?filter= shape); malformed filter → structured 422; depth/size bound enforced with structured error; narrow-never-widen board isolation contract-tested; demo: curl resolves a card by branch field.
fields.description:
Sprint 07-22 Phase 2 of docs/plans/2026-07-22-sprint-plan.md — the sprint's early user win, pulled forward so a late-sprint slip cannot zero out user value. A contract decision plus a small build, NOT mere wiring.

## Context
External clients (CLI scripts, extensions, agents) today resolve cards by grepping backlog.jsonl or relying on naming conventions. The query DSL already exists internally: CardQuery.Filter is a structured JSON DSL (internal/core/types.go:404) compiled by buildCardWhere — the same evaluator board default_filter and take-next use. The board default_filter is a hard isolation boundary (internal/core/service.go:577-579), so shape, scoping, and failure modes must be decided and pinned, not just exposed.

## Decided shape (document the decline too)
POST /v1/cards/query with body {board_id?, filter, limit?}. This deliberately DECLINES the GET /v1/cards?filter= querystring: JSON-in-URL encoding pain for the CLI/extension consumers this targets, and predicates leaking into access logs. Record the decline in docs/spec/query-dsl.md so it reads as a decision, not an omission.

## DO (contract first, then code, then pins — all in this phase)
1. **Contract**: replace query-dsl.md's "not currently wired" claim with the decided contract; document in api-surface.md. Scoping rule: with board_id, the user filter is AND-ed with the board's default_filter — it can only NARROW, never widen past board isolation; without board_id it is an explicit, documented unscoped workspace query.
2. **Implement** through the existing buildCardWhere evaluator; malformed filter → the established structured 422 path (pattern: TestTakeNextMalformedFilterIs422 in internal/httpapi/filter_test.go); add a predicate depth/size bound so a pathological filter cannot cheaply monopolize the single connection — rejected with a structured error naming the bound.
3. **Pin in the same phase (do not defer to Phase 4)**: tests for the 422 shape, the depth bound, and — critically — that board_id + user filter can only narrow, never widen. The isolation test is an exit criterion, not a follow-up.

## Demo
From plain curl or the CLI: resolve the open card whose branch field matches a PR head — no grep, no naming convention. The first thing this sprint ships is something an external client can use the same day.

## Expected outcomes / exit
- POST /v1/cards/query decided, documented, implemented through the existing evaluator.

data.title: pi-cards: read surface — list/get/search tools + text board (P0 exit)

fields.description:

- One shared `src/session.ts` state module (resolved client, actor, board, short-id cache) — later cards extend it. - Tool `execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)` — `signal`/`onUpdate` may be undefined (verified against types.d.ts).
- In `print`/`json` mode every path must work with zero prompts.

Acceptance:
- `pi -e ./src/index.ts -p "/cards"` against the demo workspace prints the 5-column text board (backlog→done) and exits 0.

data.title: take-next: retry to next candidate on a raced/lost claim

fields.description: ClaimAtomic returns nil on a lost CAS (another claimant won); TakeNext then returns empty even if other unowned cards remain, so a caller can see 'nothing available' under contention. With MaxOpenConns(1) in-process this can't happen, but cross-process (server + serverless CLI) still can. Fix: loop in ClaimAtomic/TakeNext to advance to the next candidate (bounded attempts) instead of returning nil on RowsAffected==0.

data.title: Sprint 07-12 P2b: measured file-WAL read-under-write baseline + written a/b/c go/no-go verdict

fields.description:
Phase 2 of docs/archive/2026-07-sprints/sprint-2026-07-12.md — the measured baseline that decides P3's scope (card_57e1bde9). Replaces the mis-framed 'connection-bound vs write-hold' spike with the real question.

PREREQUISITE NOTE: P2a (card_77d6c663) is DONE — the shared-cache test harness landed (test-only; production Open keeps MaxOpenConns(1) + _txlock=immediate unchanged). This card is unblocked.

DO: run a baseline against a FILE-backed WAL DB in a tempdir (matching the production Open path — :memory: has no fsync and would FAKE the verdict), driven through a transport users touch (HTTP ListCards, optionally MCP). State the load profile up front (e.g. 8 concurrent readers at a sustained write rate resembling dogfooding traffic) and record p50/p95 read latency.

DECISION RULE — written BEFORE running:
(a) reads degrade observably under write load → proceed to P3 reader pool (the single-conn serializer is _txlock=immediate + SetMaxOpenConns(1) at internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:~57);
(b) reads fine but writes stall → P3 alternate scope: reduce write-tx hold time (FTS upsert + event insert inside UpdateCard's tx, internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:~588);
(c) nothing observable → PARK P3 with the evidence recorded on the canonical read-pool card. This is a DESIGNED outcome, not a sprint failure.

| (b) reads fine, writes stall | write ack latency under same profile | write p95 degrades >2x → P3 rescope: write-tx hold time (FTS upsert + event insert) |

data.title: TRACKER: Sprint 07-22 — Solid Substrate, Demonstrated Composition

fields.description:
SPRINT TRACKER (parent) — not an implementation card. Do not implement work here; drive and close child cards. Executable detail lives on the children.

Plan of record: docs/plans/2026-07-22-sprint-plan.md
(produced by the /sprint-plan workflow: survey → align → strategy → investigation → draft → 3-lens review → revise → refine)

## Why this sprint exists

Post-v0.2.0, the last four days were pure polish; feature work is queued, not in flight. This sprint front-loads one real user-facing capability (a decided card-query endpoint), settles the one kernel question the vision can't push to an extension (SQLite concurrent reads — where a well-evidenced PARK is first-class success), pins the contract surfaces extensions ride on, then spends that trust on visible composition: runnable extension examples and a schema-authoring UI. Every phase either ships something a user notices or is honestly labeled enabling work with a rollback story.

## Children (phase map)

| Phase | Short id | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 670dab61 | Foundation hygiene: backlog.md regen, writeDefinitionAndReload seam, MCP no-reload doc, DoD rules | todo |
| P2 | 3fd62d32 | POST /v1/cards/query — contract + endpoint + isolation pins (early user win) | todo |
| P3a | 495d2e09 | (adopted from Sprint 07-12 P2b) file+WAL read-under-write baseline + written a/b/c verdict | backlog |
| P3b | 57e1bde9 | (adopted from Sprint 07-12 P3) execute the verdict: reader pool / write-hold cut / park-with-evidence | backlog |
| P4 | ad67971f | Pin contracts (OpenAPI structural, error paths, SSE filters) + drive examples fa6d5c2f, 469c93e2 | backlog |
| P5 | 0fd1b9b7 | Schema-authoring UI — create-first, additive-safe | backlog |

Order: P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5. P2 is deliberately pulled AHEAD of the SQLite work so a late slip cannot zero out user value. P4 depends on P2 (PR-sync rides the query endpoint); P5 depends on P1 (write seam) and P2 (affected-card counts).

## Standing rules (DoD — recorded here per Phase 1)

1. Any change flipping a [proposed]/[built] status anchor updates docs/reference/implementation-status.md in the SAME commit (docaudit boundary tests enforce this in CI).
2. Any phase that flips anchors carries a one-line rollback note — what reverts if the phase is cut mid-sprint — so no phase can leave the ledger half-flipped.
3. P3: park-with-evidence (verdict c) is the DEFAULT, reliability-preserving outcome — the single-conn + _txlock=immediate design is a deliberate correctness choice; branch (a) must clear a behavioral bar (read-your-own-writes race test), not just a signature bar.
4. No buildDSN/pragma abstraction before P3 branch-(a) — the moment a second DSN actually exists, not earlier.
5. P4 cut rule: contract tests land first (they gate P5); the changelog example is the cuttable tail; PR-sync stays.

## Out of scope (deliberate — declines, not omissions)

- GET /v1/cards?filter= querystring (declined in favor of POST body; documented in query-dsl.md)
- AUTH implementation (350b1bac stays parked; 2680d5f7 stays blocked on it)
- Outbox/tailer + webhooks extension (gated by outbox-gonogo.md: infrastructure ahead of need)
- Service-kind webhook receiver / making `expose` real — GitHub-Action shape is the blessed pattern
- Bulk/background/lazy-on-read schema migration — P5 pins old cards at their schema_version by contract
- MCP hot-reload mid-session — shipped scope is drift DETECTION (schema_version echo) + documented reconnect
- work_cards client convenience library; full cards-bench suite (only P3's fixtures land, in adoptable shape)
- Drag-drop lane reordering (d44d3e0d) and home/nav polish beyond what P5 templates require

## Done when

- Every child in the table is done (P3b may close as parked-with-evidence after P3a's verdict c).
- Sprint 07-12 tracker b3079e56 is CLOSED by P3 (its remaining spine is adopted here), and split-parent c7a70b64 is re-homed.
- All flipped doc anchors carry same-commit implementation-status.md updates + rollback notes.
- Sprint close: scripts/board.sh export + commit once after residual children close (never edit JSONL by hand while a server is live).

- cards get each child id above; statuses match the table or are newer-done.
- test -f docs/plans/2026-07-22-sprint-plan.md
- After P2: curl -s -X POST :8787/v1/cards/query -d '{"filter":{...}}' returns filtered cards; malformed filter → 422.
- After P3: verdict a/b/c written on 495d2e09 with measured numbers; b3079e56 closed.
- After P4: docaudit tests pass with anchors flipped; PR-sync canned-payload harness green in go test.
- After P5: create a type in /ui, create a card of it, additive-edit it — old card reads valid at its pinned schema_version.

data.title: MCP parity honesty: reflective Service enumeration, non-vacuous dry-run test, contract prose sync

fields.acceptance: Parity test reflects over core.Service (new unclassified mutation fails CI); dry-run test bites on polarity inversion; dry-run response carries dropped fields; README/SPEC prose matches behavior.
fields.description:
From the sprint 07-11 post-merge review (b23aff8) of the P2 MCP epic. The confirm gate and tools are correct; the guard-rails and contract prose around them are not.

1) MAJOR — vacuous dry-run test: TestMCPUpgradeSchema_DryRunByDefault (internal/mcp/parity_test.go:185-203) creates a card already at the type's current schema_version, so both dry-run and apply hit the no-op early-return (service.go:936). Inverting the confirm polarity at mcp.go:327 stays green. FIX: fixture with a genuinely stale schema_version so dry-run proves no mutation and confirm:true proves mutation.

2) MAJOR — parity equality not enforced: parity_test.go compares two hand-maintained lists (fixedMCPTools vs allowlist); there is no reflective enumeration of core.Service, so a future mutating method added with neither a tool nor an allowlist entry fails nothing — the exact drift this test was chartered to prevent. Currently accurate (manually verified: only unmirrored mutation is DeleteCard, allowlisted). FIX: reflect over core.Service exported methods, classify mutating vs accessor, assert tool set == mutating minus allowlist; keep one-reason-per-entry rule.

3) MINOR — dry-run response lacks the promised drop list: 'dropped' is computed (service.go:956-963) but only emitted in the SchemaUpgraded event on apply; the mcp.go:323 description says 'returns fields that would drop' — an agent will look for a nonexistent key. FIX: include dropped fields in the dry-run response.

4) MINOR — README overclaims 'mutation tools require version' (false for add_link, remove_link, add_comment, edit_comment, upgrade_schema) — costs agents a get_card round-trip. Sync prose (parity test asserts the tool list, not this sentence).

5) MINOR — blank-actor mutations: RemoveLink (service.go:1186) and EditComment (service.go:1330) lack ActorRequired unlike AddLink/AddComment/Release/UpgradeSchema; with no CARDS_USER and no default_user, MCP commits events with empty actor. Decide: add ActorRequired or document.

6) MINOR — transport divergence: REST apiUpgradeSchema applies by default (dry_run zero-value) while MCP previews by default. Intentional, but record the asymmetry in SPEC-API-SURFACE.md in one line.

VERIFY: go test ./internal/mcp; polarity-inversion mutation of mcp.go:327 makes the suite fail.

fields.description:
Most decisions this card wanted are already the lasting contract in `docs/architecture/design-system.md` § "Interactivity layer (Alpine.js)" — Alpine 3.15.0 self-hosted+embedded; Go templates own server data + first paint; Alpine owns ephemeral UI state only; `swapHTML` is the sole HTML→DOM seam; Pinemix is a *behavior* reference only (Tailwind styling always replaced); enforcement via `internal/docaudit/frontend_test.go`. Rebuild JS already has `cardsAPI` (`templates/assets/api.js`) as the sole fetch seam.

**Do not treat the prior comment as fact:** `docs/design/ADR-pinemix-reference-only.md` does not exist. `docs/plans/frontend-rebuild-plan.md` was archived to `docs/archive/2026-07-sprints/frontend-rebuild-plan.md`. Sprint note that claimed "ADR accepted" was aspirational.

## Remaining work (docs only — no kernel/UI code)

Prefer extending the existing design-system section (it already functions as the ADR) over inventing a parallel `ADR-*.md`, unless you truly need a short standalone pointer file that links there.

1. **Document `cardsAPI` as the sole fetch seam** alongside `swapHTML` in design-system (today only the code + comments say this).
2. **CSP escape hatch (one sentence):** default Alpine build assumes no CSP / needs eval; if a CSP arrives, switch to `@alpinejs/csp` (authoring impact). Note Google Fonts remote link remains known-out-of-scope if still true.
3. **One-paragraph "are we using Pinemix?" answer**, crisp enough to paste in reviews: optional *behavior* reference (patterns: open/close, roving tabindex, type-ahead); **zero** Pinemix/Tailwind CSS or package dependency; we do not import or vendor their source — so a harvest-license gate is **N/A** unless/until someone copies their source text (// HARD GATE then).
4. **Point enforcement** at the concrete docaudit guards (`TestSwapSeamIsTheOnlyInnerHTMLWrite`, x-for allowlist, Alpine present, etc.).
5. **Fix stale links:** any live doc still pointing at `docs/plans/frontend-rebuild-plan.md` should cite the archive path or the design-system section instead.

## Out of scope
JS/CSS implementation, combobox harvest work, changing Alpine build, new dependencies, status moves on child feature cards.

## Done when (observable)
- [ ] design-system (or a short ADR that only links to it) states: Alpine self-hosted; division of labor; `swapHTML` sole HTML seam; `cardsAPI` sole fetch seam; Pinemix reference-only + license N/A unless source harvest; CSP → `@alpinejs/csp` escape hatch; docaudit as enforcement.

data.title: Sprint 07-19 P2: JSONL snapshot residual gaps (CLI wrapper, byte-stability, frozen fixture, board.sh smoke)

fields.description:
## What shipped

Board snapshots are now locked down by tests. Exporting a board and importing it again is verified byte-for-byte against a frozen fixture, so the `backlog.jsonl` file committed to git will restore the exact same board on any machine — no drift, no surprises. Nothing changed in the product itself; this is pure safety net.

---

Phase 2 of docs/plans/2026-07-19-sprint-plan.md — contract pinning. The headline round-trip is ALREADY pinned by `cmd/cards/portable_test.go` (commit `3236f3d`, 7 tests: full fidelity, state-only, pagination, failure modes). This phase adds only the 4 genuine residual gaps, against a frozen hash-pinned fixture (NOT the live board). No production code changed unless a named non-determinism fix is required.

## DO
1. **CLI wrapper coverage.** Extend `cmd/cards/portable_test.go` with cases exercising `exportCmd`/`importCmd` flag parsing (`--out`/`--in` file IO) and the fresh-DB pre-flight refusal (`cmd/cards/import.go:52`). Reuse `openWorkspace`/`dbPath` (`cmd/cards/open.go`).
2. **Re-export byte-stability (named ordering guarantee).** `TestExportStateOnlyByteStable`: export → import → re-export → byte-compare. The guarantee under test is the id-sorted canonical ordering applied by `portable.go`'s INLINE `slices.SortFunc` calls (users `:58` / cards `:93` / events `:118` — there are NO named `sortCards`/`sortUsers`/`sortEvents` functions; the sort is inline). If byte-stability is already guaranteed by those sort calls, the test is a pin (regression guard). If a non-determinism source is found (map iteration in event metadata, field ordering), the fix belongs in `portable.go` — name it in the test comment. Diff sorted line sets, not raw bytes, so a future failure fails diagnostically.
3. **Frozen, hash-pinned fixture.** Copy `.cards/backlog.jsonl` at sprint start to `cmd/cards/testdata/backlog.frozen.jsonl`. Test loads the frozen copy, asserts a sha256 computed at freeze time and pinned in the test. The live `.cards/backlog.jsonl` is NOT a test input. Silent fixture drift trips a loud single-line failure printing the regeneration command, not a 190-card diff.
4. **`board.sh` smoke under `go test`.** `TestBoardScriptSmoke` (a Go test shelling out, NOT a standalone bash script) covering `board.sh import --force` and `install-hook` in a temp repo so `install-hook` does not clobber the real `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. Runs under `go test ./...`, not a forgotten CI step.

## ACCEPTANCE (binary)
- [ ] CLI wrapper flag IO + fresh-DB refusal under test.
- [ ] Re-export byte-stable (sorted-line diff); ordering guarantee named (id-sorted canonical via `portable.go` inline `slices.SortFunc` at `:58`/`:93`/`:118`, or a named non-determinism fix in `portable.go`).
- [ ] Test fixture version-pinned: `cmd/cards/testdata/backlog.frozen.jsonl` with sha256 asserted in test; live board is not a test input.
- [ ] `board.sh import --force` + `install-hook` smoked via `go test` (shelling out), in a temp repo.
- [ ] No production code changed unless a named non-determinism fix was required; `go test ./cmd/cards` green.

## DEMO
`go test ./cmd/cards -run 'TestExportStateOnlyByteStable|TestImportFrozenBacklogSnapshot|TestBoardScriptSmoke' -v` PASS; `sha256sum cmd/cards/testdata/backlog.frozen.jsonl` matches the hash pinned in the test.

data.title: Sprint 07-12 P3: reader pool (or write-hold reduction), proven on file+WAL — CANONICAL read-pool card

fields.description:
PLAIN: today every read queues behind one write connection; this card ships a reader pool (or, if measurement says reads aren't the pain, a write-hold reduction) so multi-agent concurrency stops serializing on a single SQLite handle.

Phase 3 of docs/archive/2026-07-sprints/sprint-2026-07-12.md — CANONICAL read-pool card (reconciled from the duplicate sprawl in P1c; staged-plan evidence lives on the closed planning card card_fec18019). Ship whichever concurrency fix P2b's measurement selected — the sprint does not collapse to hygiene.

PRIMARY SCOPE (P2b verdict a): a reader pool so reads stop queueing behind the single writer.
1) Split Open into two handles: writer keeps the current DSN (_txlock=immediate, MaxOpenConns(1)); reader pool gets a DSN WITHOUT _txlock=immediate, opened read-only (mode=ro or query_only) so a misrouted write fails loudly. Sequence: open writer → Ping → Init/migrate (establishes WAL) → THEN construct the reader pool with matching busy_timeout/foreign_keys. Pool-size knob (env/config); size 1 restores today's serialized behavior (runtime escape hatch). Centralize pragma construction (two DSNs = pragma-drift risk). core.Store doc comment: migrations writer-only; readers see last committed WAL snapshot; read-your-own-writes needs the writer; cross-process immediate-tx discipline unchanged.
2) COMPLETE audit table — every Store method in exactly one column (exit criterion). Readers on pool: ListCards, CountCards, GetCard, GetCardsByShortID, ListLinks, AllLinks, Blockers, BlockingDependents, ListComments, comment counts, EventQuery List/Page, ListUsers, + advisory check-then-act reads ConditionFired (sqlite.go:1066) and GetIdempotency (sqlite.go:1154) — safe on pool ONLY because the authoritative guard is the in-tx INSERT-OR-IGNORE rowcount / writer-side upsert (note this). Writer: Insert/Update/DeleteCard, ClaimAtomic, link/comment writes, event Append, idempotency writes, user upserts, migrations. Audit SEQUENCES: any write-then-reread-to-render path reads through the writer; give reader helpers a queryer interface (pool or tx) so query code isn't forked. Note: UpdateCard's conflict re-read inside its own immediate tx makes a stale pool GetCard yield a normal version_conflict — no new hazard.
3) Prove on file+WAL (not memory): (i) regression test, tempdir WAL, N readers return while a writer holds the write lock, race-clean; (ii) freshness test — create a card through the normal handler path, immediately re-read, assert fresh version; (iii) re-run the P2b benchmark for after-numbers.

ALTERNATE SCOPE (P2b verdict b): instead of the pool, reduce UpdateCard write-tx hold time (move FTS upsert/event-insert out of the critical section where safe); prove with the same before/after benchmark. The harness (P2a), audit table, and doc-comment work still land.

IF P2b verdict c (park): record the evidence here and close as "not needed yet" — the harness + baseline ARE the deliverable.

ACCEPTANCE: reader DSN has no _txlock=immediate and is read-only (misrouted write fails loudly, asserted); audit table complete (every method one column, sequences + advisory reads annotated); concurrent-reader + read-your-own-writes freshness tests pass race-clean on file+WAL; measured p50/p95 improvement over the P2b baseline via a transport users touch.

data.title: Supervisor hardening: WaitDelay on service children, bounded log sink, startup dup race

fields.description:
From the sprint 07-11 post-merge review (b23aff8) of the P5 service supervisor. Two production-hang/memory risks plus two small races — all targeted fixes in the existing structure.

1) MAJOR — no cmd.WaitDelay on service children: runServiceOnce (internal/hooks/services.go:167-230) pipes stdout/stderr but never sets cmd.WaitDelay; the hook path sets 5s at hooks.go:226 for exactly this. A service that daemonizes a setsid grandchild inheriting stdout makes cmd.Wait block forever after SIGKILL (pgroup miss): the unbounded <-done at services.go:267 means cards serve never exits on Ctrl-C, and the same hang in stopOne (reconcile.go:175) wedges reconcileMu — every later reload/board-create HTTP handler blocks. FIX: set WaitDelay on service cmds and/or bound the post-SIGKILL <-done.

2) MAJOR — unbounded memory for chatty services: services.go:186-188 accumulates the child's entire stdout/stderr in bytes.Buffers, flushed to .cards/logs/<id>.log only at exit. Long-running services grow supervisor RSS without bound. FIX: bounded ring buffer or streaming file sink (hooks stay as-is — one-shot buffering is fine there).

3) MINOR race — duplicate supervised children at startup: Run publishes s.svcCtx (hooks.go:130) before startAutostartServices takes reconcileMu (services.go:91); a reload in that window has Reconcile start every autostart service, then startAutostartServices startOnes them all again (no already-managed check, services.go:93-96) — two supervised copies of the same id, permanently. FIX: assign svcCtx under reconcileMu, or make startOne skip ids already in s.services.

4) MINOR test flake (observed once under -race): TestReconcileAddedStarts — waitServicePID returns at pid registration, which can precede bash writing the marker; stat-once then fails. FIX: poll for the marker.

VERIFY: go test -race ./internal/hooks ./cmd/cards; new test for a SIGTERM-ignoring child with an out-of-pgroup descendant holding stdout returning within grace+WaitDelay.

2) Bounded drains: stopAllServices + stopOne post-SIGKILL waits bounded by a second drainTimeout with a loud leak log — shutdown and reconcileMu can no longer hang on an unreapable child.

data.title: Bug: board filter stalls after several rapid changes (SSE connection churn)

fields.description:
REPORTED (review): changing a board's Type filter several times in a row makes filtering stop responding; further filter changes have no effect until, after some seconds, the backend 'recovers' and the board finally updates.

DIAGNOSIS (root cause, code-verified):
- Board filter controls (Owner/Type/Sort) do a FULL-PAGE GET navigation (board.html: select onchange='this.form.submit()'). Every page load opens a NEW EventSource to /v1/events/stream (board.html SSE script).
- The SSE handler (internal/httpapi/sse.go) cleans up correctly on ctx.Done(), BUT the browser does not tear down the old EventSource instantly on navigation, and the server only notices a dead SSE connection on its next write. With HTTP/1.1's ~6-connections-per-host limit, a handful of rapid filter navigations saturate the connection pool with half-dead SSE streams, so the next navigation's requests block until an old connection is reaped -> 'recovers after time'.
- Aggravated by two things: (a) SQLite SetMaxOpenConns(1) serializes every board render through one connection; (b) the board SSE script re-fetches the WHOLE board (fetch(window.location.href)) on EVERY event, so event bursts pile DB-bound requests on top of the filter navigations.

FIX OPTIONS (cheap -> structural):
1. SSE heartbeat: emit ': keepalive' every ~15-20s so a write to a dead connection fails fast, the handler returns + unsubscribes, and the slot frees promptly (directly shrinks 'recovers after time'). Cheapest, high value.
2. Stop the connection churn: make filter changes an htmx partial swap (hx-get -> swap #board) instead of full-page nav, so ONE SSE connection persists across filter changes.
3. Debounce/coalesce the SSE-driven full-board refetch so event bursts don't stack DB-bound requests.
4. SQLite read pool (see card_fec1801913 / ROADMAP §3) removes the single-connection serialization.

Recommend 1+3 first (small, safe), then 2. Acceptance: rapidly change the Type filter 10x in a row -> the board keeps updating with no multi-second stall; SSE connections do not accumulate (verify server logs / netstat).

comments.author: jeremy
comments.body: FIXED in rebuild Phase 9 (commit 1af2dc2, card card_93ef776d57004034a50ee8057e2be4ae). Root causes addressed: (a) the persistent EventSource is now decoupled from filter navigation — $store.live is ONE connection for the page lifetime; filter changes fragment-swap the board via X-Cards-Partial without touching SSE. Verified: 20 rapid filter changes → same EventSource instance, status stays open. (b) Server-side keepalive as a ticker case in the SAME single-writer for/select (~20s ':keepalive'): a dead peer fails fast on the next write, freeing the bus slot promptly and shrinking the 'recovers after time' tail. Pinned by TestSSEKeepalive. Also delivered: reactive drag-drop, board_fragment partial, debounced swapBoard on live events, exponential-backoff reconnect with ?since=<lastId>.

data.title: Sprint 07-10 P2: AUTH.md (proposed) — identity & attribution: review + ROADMAP §1 link

fields.description:
Phase 2 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-10.md. STATUS 2026-07-10: the RFC has been WRITTEN and FROZEN as docs/design/AUTH.md (status: proposed), drafted alongside docs/design/CORE-BOUNDARIES.md and hardened through two adversarial review passes. This card no longer carries the spec content — the doc is the single source of truth (see docs/NOTES.md freeze entry).

WHAT THE DOC SETTLES (headline only — read AUTH.md):
- Identity attribution is a core concern; access control is the host's. Overlay principle at §0.
- Mode matrix: --auth none (YOLO default) | token (bearer, verified writes) | proxy (trusted header from reverse proxy).
- POST /v1/users issues an opaque bearer token (hash-only storage, no GET endpoint, rotate = revoke+reissue).
- Four adapters: HTTP middleware, CLI (credentials file / CARDS_TOKEN), MCP (token at process spawn), hooks (pass-through, no authn).
- Anti-spoof: X-Work-Cards-Actor MUST NOT beat verified identity. Actor must be a registered User.ID under token/proxy; free string under none.
- Bootstrap: serverless CLI register is always trusted (filesystem > HTTP); first-user-admin stopgap for HTTP registration under token.
- Reads open / writes verified in v0; identity resolves BEFORE idempotency replay.
- Force policy is NOT here — it lives in CORE-BOUNDARIES §3.3 + the transitions RFC card (card_f570b35b); auth keeps only the invariant that forced writes still attribute the verified actor.

REMAINING WORK ON THIS CARD (small):
1) Review request on AUTH.md — post for review, capture verdicts here.
2) Add the ROADMAP §1 cross-link to docs/design/AUTH.md.
3) On acceptance: confirm card_350b1bac (reference impl) matches the doc, then this card closes.

FROZEN: AUTH.md changes only via impl PRs that discover reality or an explicit re-open from the owner. PHILOSOPHY §1/§7 edits land WITH the first token-mode implementation, not before.

data.title: Sprint 07-22 P1: foundation hygiene — write-seam extraction, MCP no-reload doc, DoD rules

fields.description:
Sprint 07-22 Phase 1 of docs/plans/2026-07-22-sprint-plan.md — cheap, verdict-independent cleanups every later phase pays for. Honest enabling work: no user demo here by design.

## Context
v0.2.0 shipped and was polished; the board is between sprints. Before the sprint's user-facing work starts, clear four taxes: a stale committed overview, a write-path pattern about to be needed twice, an undocumented MCP limitation Phase 5 will make user-visible, and two definition-of-done rules that keep later phases from stranding half-flipped docs.

## DO (in order)
1. **Regenerate `.cards/backlog.md`** from backlog.jsonl (pi-cards export writes it) so the committed overview stops listing the already-closed release card 30026459 under `### backlog` (it is status:done in the jsonl).
2. **Extract `writeDefinitionAndReload`**: pull the write→validate→rollback→reload pattern out of `reloadableApp.handleCreateBoard` (cmd/cards/reload.go:275) into a shared helper owning the mu / selfWriteGate / reloadLocked (reload.go:158) sequence; re-express board-create on top of it. This helper is the documented seam where Phase 5's old-vs-new card-type diff check will live — it is the only layer holding both the prior and new definition generations (validateCardType cannot diff).
3. **Document the `cards mcp` no-reload limitation** in docs/extensions/mcp.md: tool schemas are baked at process construction (mcpCmd, cmd/cards/serve.go:192), stdio MCP has no server-push channel, so definition edits do not reach a live agent session — recovery is reconnect; additive-optional-with-default schema edits are what keep a stale agent's in-flight writes valid.
4. **Record two DoD rules on the sprint tracker** (parent card): (a) any change flipping a [proposed]/[built] anchor updates docs/reference/implementation-status.md in the SAME commit (docaudit enforces in CI); (b) any anchor-flipping phase carries a one-line rollback note — what reverts if the phase is cut mid-sprint.

## Explicitly NOT in this phase
No buildDSN/pragma extraction — today exactly one production site builds pragmas (sqlite.Open, internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:35); extracting now is speculative abstraction. It moves into Phase 3 branch-(a), gated on the measurement verdict actually requiring a second DSN.

## Expected outcomes / exit
- backlog.md section membership matches backlog.jsonl status for every card (30026459 under done).
- handleCreateBoard is a thin caller of writeDefinitionAndReload; reload tests (cmd/cards/reload_test.go) stay green; mutex/self-write semantics live in exactly one place.
- MCP staleness + reconnect recovery + additive-edit validity stated in docs/extensions/mcp.md.
- Both DoD lines written on the tracker card.

fields.description:
From the sprint 07-11 post-merge review (b23aff8) of the P4 style_field epic. Core feature is correct and leak-free; two edges break its guarantees, and the dogfood/demo is invisible.

1) MAJOR — nondeterministic modal theming: boardForCard (internal/httpapi/render.go:603-610) iterates the s.boards MAP and returns the first board containing the card's type; renderCardDetail/uiCardModal feed that into resolveCardTheme. With a type on two boards where only one sets style_field, the modal randomly shows option-theme or type-theme per request (Go map order); the modal URL carries no board context, so 'same card renders differently on two boards' fails in the modal. Demo unaffected today (one board per type). FIX: deterministic board choice (sorted ids) as a floor; better, thread board context into the modal fetch (board page already knows it).

2) MAJOR — dark-scheme contrast hole in labels/journal themes: those themes use the option muted wash as the FULL card background with color: var(--c-text) (style.css:1141-1142 journal, 1384-1385 labels); in dark mode --c-text is #e9ebed on light pastel muted = ~1.2:1. Repro: engineering + ?theme=labels + OS dark + card with kind set. The 4.5:1 load floor only checks accent-on-muted. Related: labels paints fixed #fffdf5/#fffdf7 icon ON accent (style.css:1393, 1472) — legal pairs give ~1.3:1 there. FIX options: theme-scoped rule keeping text tokens off option-washed surfaces, or extend the floor to text-on-muted + fixed-on-accent pairs. Related card: the accent-contrast-floor card (a11y follow-up).

3) MINOR — option-theme render branch not golden-pinned + dogfood invisible: no golden fixture sets kind, and 0 of 50 programming-tasks in the demo have kind set — the shipped board renders identically to pre-style_field. FIX: one kind-set fixture + golden; backfill kind on a handful of dogfood cards so the feature is visible.

4) TRIVIAL — ParseHexColor doc comment (contrast.go:15) claims linear sRGB but returns gamma-encoded (linearization is in RelativeLuminance). Comment fix.

data.title: Export bundle: cards export --with-artifacts (portable workspace incl. artifact bytes)

fields.description:
## What shipped

A board can now travel whole. `cards export --with-artifacts` writes the referenced attachment bytes (sha256-verified) beside the snapshot, and `cards import --with-artifacts` restores them into a fresh workspace — so screenshots and evidence files survive the move to another machine instead of dangling. Any corrupt or missing blob fails the transfer loudly. `board.sh` uses it automatically, which also means every committed attachment is re-verified on each board sync.

---

Today the snapshot carries artifact pointers ({uri, mime, size, sha256}) but artifacts/ is gitignored and bytes stay machine-local, so links dangle on a fresh clone. Add an opt-in bundle export/import that includes artifact bytes (content-addressed, sha256-verified) for full workspace hand-off.

The LFS / uri-policy alternatives are already documented (docs/using-cards.md 'Artifacts'); this card is the bundle path for when you want a single self-contained portable workspace.

SCOPE: a new flag (e.g. cards export --with-artifacts) that, alongside the JSONL state, writes artifact bytes keyed by sha256; a matching import that restores them into the target workspace's artifacts/ root and verifies sha256 on read. Reuses the existing artifact_policy: local confinement path (internal/artifacts). Opt-in — default export stays pointer-only.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the artifact field shape; auto-fetching uri-policy artifacts; bundling non-artifact workspace files.

DONE WHEN: cards export --with-artifacts produces a bundle whose artifact bytes round-trip through cards import into a fresh workspace; a sha256 mismatch on import fails loudly; existing pointer-only export/import is unchanged; docs/using-cards.md 'Artifacts' notes the bundle flag.

VERIFY: round-trip — cards export --with-artifacts to a tempdir, fresh workspace, cards import, assert artifact links resolve and sha256 verifies; assert a tampered byte fails import loudly.

**Validated**
- Snapshot carries artifact pointers `{uri, mime, size, sha256}`; `artifacts/` is gitignored and bytes are machine-local — confirmed in `docs/using-cards.md` 'Artifacts' and `internal/artifacts/`.
- `artifact_policy: "local"` confinement path exists (`internal/artifacts/artifacts.go`, `internal/core/service.go:1276`) and is reused correctly by this proposal.
- LFS / uri-policy alternatives are already documented ('Artifacts' section) — the card's "done in docs" claim is accurate.
- No `--with-artifacts` / bundle code exists today (grep confirms) — genuine gap.

**Issues found**
- No done-when or observable verify — only a prose description.
- Did not state opt-in vs default clearly, nor that the artifact field shape is unchanged.

**Changes made**
- Added SCOPE / OUT OF SCOPE / DONE WHEN / VERIFY sections.
- Made opt-in explicit (default export stays pointer-only).
- Pinned reuse of the existing `artifact_policy: local` confinement path.
- Added observable verify: round-trip into a fresh workspace, sha256 verifies, tampered bytes fail loudly, pointer-only path unchanged.

**Scope verdict**: keep-as-is — one opt-in flag with a matching import; correctly narrow.
**Arch verdict**: aligned — content-addressed sha256-verified bytes, reuses the existing confinement path, no field-shape change; matches philosophy §2 (files where they help) and §10 (boring tech).

data.title: Home & app-nav polish: counts, wayfinding, brand mark

fields.description:
Make the workspace home and top nav feel like a finished product shell — so someone opening Cards can see how busy each board is, always know how to get Home, and recognize the app at a glance.

## Already true (do not redo)
- `GET /` already renders the real home page (`home.html` via `uiIndex`) — board list, workspace totals, recent activity. No redirect fix needed.
- App nav already has brand → `/`, a board picker that acts as a breadcrumb trail, `+ New Card`, and `+ New board` inside the picker.
- Board kanban layout is out of scope.

## Ship these four edges

### 1. Per-board card counts on the home grid
Each home board card today shows only column count and type count. Add the number of cards on that board (e.g. `12 cards · 5 columns · 3 types`). Workspace-level total in the hero can stay. Verify with a 1-board workspace and a many-board workspace.

### 2. Clearer Home wayfinding from a board
On `/ui/boards/:id`, users should not have to guess that the brand is Home. Keep the existing `Brand / Board` crumb pattern, but make Home explicit (label, title/aria, or a dedicated Home segment — pick the lightest change that reads clearly). Do not add a second competing nav system.

### 3. Stronger brand mark in `.app-nav`
Replace or back the unicode `▚` with a small mono app mark (mask-icon or inline SVG) that follows design-system rules: `currentColor`, token-sized, theme-safe, no emoji, no per-theme markup forks. Works on the always-dark nav ink bar.

### 4. Home hero quick actions
On the home hero only, surface **New card** and **New board** using the existing modal create links (`data-create-link` → `/ui/cards/new/modal`, `/ui/boards/new/modal`). Nav CTAs stay; hero actions help empty/first-run and multi-board scanning.

## Constraints
- Templates/CSS only in app shell + home — no kanban redesign, no new framework, no design-system violations (containers own spacing; roles/tokens for type; themes remap tokens).
- Parent wave `86515fd2` marks this PARKED / out of current sprint — fine to implement later; do not block in-sprint work.
- Prefer one small PR.

## Done when
1. Home board cards show an accurate per-board card count alongside existing meta; checked for 1-board and many-board workspaces.
2. From a board view, a sighted user and a screen-reader user can reach Home without relying on tribal knowledge that the word "Cards" is the link.
3. `.app-nav` shows a distinct mono brand mark that survives theme changes and matches design-system icon guidance.
4. Home hero offers New card and New board actions that open the existing create modals.
5. `go test ./internal/httpapi` passes; hard-refresh shows embedded template/CSS changes.

## Out of scope
- Reworking GET `/` routing (already correct).
- Recent-activity redesign, search changes, board kanban, header IA beyond wayfinding/brand.
- Live SSE updates on the home page.
