data.title: pi-cards: write surface — create/update/comment/claim/release/take_next + config (P1)

fields.description:
pi-cards series 4/8 — write surface + config file (P1). Spec §5.5, §6.3 rows 4-9, §7. Blocked by card 3 (read surface).

Read surface is live; this completes P1: the LLM can round-trip a card from chat with full write honesty (§5.5). Also lands `.pi/cards.json` / `~/.pi/agent/cards.json` config loading (§7) and auto-registration of the agent actor.

Scope:
- `src/config.ts`: read user then project `cards.json`, project wins; env overrides per §7 table; defaults `autoExport:"off"`, `worklogOnTurn:false`, `work.batchLimit:3`, `work.autoDone:false`. (pi has no per-extension settings API — read the JSON files directly.)
- `src/tools-write.ts`: `cards_create` (`type_id`, `title`, `fields`, `tags`, `dry_run`; validation errors returned verbatim incl. `valid_options`), `cards_update` (fields/status/owner/tags, `version` + §5.5 retry, `dry_run`), `cards_comment` (markdown body, actor attributed), `cards_append_entry` (repeating fields), `cards_claim`/`cards_release` (409 surfaces current owner), `cards_take_next` (`status`/`type_id`/`board_id` filters; on `{card:null}` re-issue once to disambiguate race vs empty per api-surface §11).
- First write per session auto-registers the actor: `POST /v1/users` kind `agent` (HTTP) / `cards users register` (CLI), ignoring "already exists" (§5.4).
- Tool results return the server's updated card, never assumed local state.

Implementation notes:
- `dry_run` passes through; CLI backend forwards `--dry-run` where the verb supports it (confirmed on create/patch only — degrade loudly on other verbs, per spec-gap finding).
- CLI release uses the `patch --owner ""` mapping validated in card 2.
- Board transitions are enforced server-side (engineering board `enforce_transitions:true`); do not pre-validate in the extension beyond surfacing the structured error.
- CLI `claim` requires `--version N` — fetch version via `cards_get` first (preflight pattern).

Acceptance:
- `pi -e ./src/index.ts -p "create a programming-task card titled X with branch feat/x, then move it to todo"` against a throwaway copy of the fixture workspace: card created, appears in `cards list`, status todo.
- Forced conflict: patch with a stale `version` → visible `version_conflict`, single auto-retry succeeds on fresh version (unit + integration test).
- `cards_take_next --status todo` claims oldest unowned card as the resolved actor (actorSuffix applied); a second call gets the next card or null.
- `node --test` + typecheck green; config precedence covered by a unit test (project beats user beats env-default).

Out of scope: typed `cards_create_<type>` generated tools (card 8); `cards_history`/`cards_breaches`/`cards_events` (phase-2); worklog automation (cards 6-7).

data.title: Design: user-defined columns/card-types — how far does the UI go?

fields.description:
QUESTION (review): when creating a board, columns and card types look fixed. Are they user-definable (CLI/web), and how far do we take the UI — visual schema editing, or just files?

CURRENT STATE (code-verified):
- Columns and card types ARE user-defined — at the WORKSPACE level, in git-backed files: workspace.json 'columns', and definitions/card-types/<id>.json. Boards reference SUBSETS.
- The create-board modal (board_create.html) intentionally offers CHECKBOXES of EXISTING workspace columns + existing card types; validateBoard enforces board.columns subset-of workspace.columns and card_type_ids reference existing types. That's why they look 'fixed' — a board composes existing building blocks, it can't invent columns/types inline.
- Adding a NEW column = edit workspace.json; a NEW card type = add a card-types/*.json file; then reload. No UI for that yet. (create-a-board already WRITES a reviewable definitions/boards/<id>.json — the 'UI writes files' pattern.)

DIRECTION (per PHILOSOPHY.md #2 Files-where-they-help, #3 Schemas-not-magic, #6 Extensions-over-plugins):
- Schemas stay explicit, versioned, git-backed FILES. The UI's job is to WRITE/EDIT those files (as create-a-board does), not to become the source of truth.
- Recommended middle ground: a board/workspace settings editor + a card-type editor that generate/patch the JSON files (reviewable, diffable, reload-applied). Already partially queued as card 'UI: board settings editor'.
- A full drag-and-drop visual schema BUILDER leans toward extension territory — it can be an external process talking to the API, keeping the core small.

DECISION NEEDED: how far in-core? (a) files only + docs; (b) settings/type editors that write JSON (recommended); (c) full visual schema designer (probably an extension). Deliverable once decided: scope + wire the chosen editors; document in DESIGN.md + SPEC presentation.

data.title: Census follow-ups: unclamped paging for item-iterating scans + DefaultFilter board membership

fields.description:
Deferred from Sprint P2 (column-census fix). P2 fixed ONLY the scalar count in `countColumn` via `Store.CountCards` (COUNT(*)) — see service.go:190. Two related truncation/correctness gaps remain, intentionally out of P2 scope because they need row iteration, not a scalar count:

**1. Item-iterating scans still capped at 500.** These build per-card deadlines/items, so `COUNT(*)` does NOT apply; they need unclamped or cursor paging:
- `internal/core/service.go:345` — `MaxTimeInStatus` scan (`ListCards{Status, TypeIDIn, Limit:500}` per status). A board with >500 cards in a watched status can miss `status_timeout` deadlines.
- `internal/core/service.go:392` — `rebuildCardIdle` scan (`ListCards{TypeIDIn, Limit:500}`). Can miss `card_idle` deadlines on large boards.
- `internal/core/breaches.go:130` — blocked-card scan (`CardQuery{Blocked:true, Limit:breachScanLimit}` where `breachScanLimit=500`, breaches.go:52). Under-lists blocked cards.

**2. DefaultFilter board-membership gap** (pre-existing, still documented in the `countColumn` caveat at service.go:~156, and mirrored at breaches.go:67): `countColumn` counts membership by `TypeIDIn` (board.CardTypeIDs) only. A board scoped by `DefaultFilter` instead of card types is not counted correctly for WIP/lane census. Revisit only if a filter-defined board needs WIP/lane limits.

**Done when:** the three scans page without a silent 500 cap (cursor-paged or explicit unclamped with a documented bound), each with a >500-row regression test that asserts no deadline/blocked-card is dropped; `countColumn` honors DefaultFilter-scoped boards OR the caveat is converted to an explicit 'unsupported' error returned to the caller (fail loudly, principle 9). `clampCardLimit`'s ListCards ceiling for normal paged reads stays unchanged.

fields.description:
PLAIN: type-name badges paint text in the author's accent color, and several shipped accents fail WCAG AA contrast against their background. Fix badge text contrast without redesigning the badge or losing author palette.

Found during the P4 a11y pass (card_25023962). .card__type-badge paints the type name in the author-defined accent on the muted wash; several shipped type themes fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 — e.g. frontend-task #cf7b00 on #f6e7cc ≈ 2.65:1 (axe: serious).

WHY NOT FIXED THEN: a11y pass forbade visual redesign; colors are TypeTheme author identity.

STATUS UPDATE (style_field landed): card_8b3e83d9 (style_field legibility) is DONE — OptionThemes now ship on programming-task (feature/bug/design/infra) on the same --card-stock / badge seam. A badge-only CSS hotfix that ignores that path will re-regress the day a monotype board turns on presentation.style_field. This card is now the residual a11y contrast work on top of the landed schema.

DECISION REQUIRED (pick one; document in docs/design/style-field.md a11y section):
A) RUNTIME TEXT SHADE — keep author accent/muted for washes + spine; derive badge TEXT from a contrast-safe shade against --card-stock-bg so author palette stays, text always AA.
B) LOAD-TIME FLOOR — validate TypeTheme + OptionThemes accent/muted pairs at definition load (structured error: which field, which value, 4.5:1 required). Fits Phase 2 validation platform; warn-tier first for legacy accents if needed.
C) Hybrid: B for new option_themes, A as residual safety for existing soft accents.

RECOMMEND: C if budget allows; else A alone unblocks demo types without waiting on authors.

ACCEPT:
- All demo TypeThemes (and style_field option_themes, now dogfooded on programming-task) pass 4.5:1 for badge text on wash in light AND dark (prefers-color-scheme).
- No layout change to .card__type-badge geometry (WYSIWYG edit chrome unchanged).
- Decision written in docs/design/style-field.md a11y section; load-time path if chosen uses structured errors.
- Test coverage: contrast helper and/or fixture table of shipped accents.

OUT: redesigning the badge; a second token namespace; color-only meaning (icon stays mandatory under style_field).

Surface: theme. Coordinate with style_field before claiming 'contrast holds' as a Phase 4 exit criterion alone.

data.title: Fix idempotency: wrong actor + schema PK allows cross-actor overwrite

fields.description: Two compounding bugs. (1) The idempotent() wrapper calls actorFromCtx() which reads context+default user, but withActor() hasn't run yet (idempotent is the OUTER wrapper), so lookup/record always use default_user regardless of X-Work-Cards-Actor header. Fix: use resolveActor() (reads header/env/default) in the idempotent wrapper. (2) idempotency_keys PK is `key` only; GetIdempotency filters key+actor but INSERT OR REPLACE overwrites another actor's row for the same key. Fix: PRIMARY KEY (key, actor). Add tests with X-Work-Cards-Actor != default user.

work_log.author: pi
work_log.notes: Fixed two compounding bugs: (1) wrapper order was idempotent(withActor(...)) — idempotent ran before withActor set the context, so actor was always default_user. Swapped to withActor(idempotent(...)). (2) idempotency_keys PK was just (key) — two actors with the same key collided. Changed to composite PK (key, actor). Regression test: TestIdempotencyActorScoping verifies two actors with the same key get distinct cards, and replay is scoped per actor. Verified end-to-end against live server.

comments.author: foz
comments.body: Verified. Routes: s.idempotent(s.withActor(...)) — idempotent is OUTER, runs before withActor sets the context. idempotent() calls s.actorFromCtx(r) which reads core.ActorFromCtx (context) → falls back to default_user, ignoring X-Work-Cards-Actor. So all idempotency records are scoped to default_user. Schema: idempotency_keys PK is `key` only (sqlite.go:103); GetIdempotency filters key+actor but PutIdempotency uses INSERT OR REPLACE on key → overwrites cross-actor. Existing test passes only because it uses 'local-dev' (the default user). Fix: (1) use resolveActor() in idempotent wrapper; (2) PRIMARY KEY (key, actor).

data.title: pi-cards: git board persistence + interim worklog activity (P4a)

fields.description:
pi-cards series 7/8 — git board persistence + interim worklog activity (P4a). Spec §6.6, §6.7. Blocked by card 6 (execution).

Execution lands activity on cards; this adds G5 and the worklog-on-turn option: board state rides in git via the CLI exporter, never hand-written, with opt-in auto-export cadences.

Scope:
- `src/sync.ts`: `exportBoard()` — if `<workspace repo>/scripts/board.sh` exists, shell out to `board.sh export`; else run `cards export --state-only --out <workspace>/backlog.jsonl` directly; then `git add backlog.jsonl && git commit -m "cards: board sync (<n> cards)"`, guarded by `git diff --quiet` (commit only when the export changed something). Never push.
- `/cards export` command; board UI `g` key wired to it.
- Auto mode per config `autoExport`: `"shutdown"` → `session_shutdown` hook; `"idle"` → debounced `agent_settled` hook firing only after any `cards_*` mutation this session (track a dirty flag in `session.ts`); `"off"` default.
- `worklogOnTurn:true` → debounced `turn_end` handler: while a card is claimed by this session and `git log --oneline` shows new commits since the last entry, append an interim `work_log` note via `cards_append_entry`. Default off; close-out entries from card 6 unaffected.

Implementation notes:
- All git ops via `pi.exec("git", [...], {timeout})` in the workspace repo root; surface stderr verbatim on failure, never retry a commit.
- `backlog.jsonl` is written only by the exporter (repo rule, §6.6) — no manual edits anywhere in the extension.
- Shutdown hook must be fast and non-interactive: skip export if backend resolution failed this session.

Acceptance:
- In a git-initialized fixture repo: mutate a card, run `pi -e ./src/index.ts -p "/cards export"` → `git log --oneline` shows `cards: board sync (<n> cards)` and the exported `backlog.jsonl` re-imports into a fresh workspace successfully.
- Second `/cards export` with no changes → no new commit (diff-quiet guard).
- `autoExport:"shutdown"` config → session exit produces the commit; `worklogOnTurn:true` + a commit mid-run → interim work_log entry visible on the card.
- `node --test` + typecheck green (git ops unit-tested against a temp repo).

Out of scope: auto-push, PR creation, pre-commit hook installation (board.sh's job, user's choice); conflict resolution for diverged `backlog.jsonl`.

data.title: Security: escape/validate filter key paths in the filter DSL (SQL injection)

fields.acceptance: Filter key outside [A-Za-z0-9_] (after optional fields. prefix) → validation_failed on field 'filter' (HTTP 400), never reaches SQLite; legit fields.<id> and bare-field filters unchanged; regression test bites without the fix. go test ./internal/sqlite green.
fields.description:
Found by the Copilot review of PR #18 (https://github.com/somebox/cards/pull/18#issuecomment-4935628132), verified real.

PROBLEM: internal/sqlite/filter.go columnExpr interpolated a client-supplied filter key straight into the '$.<id>' JSON-path string literal with no escaping. The VALUE side is parameterized (?), but the PATH side was not. A filter key like fields.x') OR 1=1-- broke out of the literal — confirmed by a temporary test run producing 'SQL logic error: incomplete input' and 'near ";": syntax error'. Pre-existing on main; the new $has operator (Phase 3) extended the same pattern. Not exploitable under YOLO/local-only trust, but the filter DSL is a public API surface and should land before --auth token (AUTH.md).

FIX: validate the field-id portion of the key against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ (mirrors core.sortFieldRE in sort.go) before interpolation; reject anything else as a filter validation error (surfaces as HTTP 400). Collapses the fields.<id> and bare-key branches through one guard. Legit keys unchanged.

TEST: three injection/invalid keys added to TestFilterDSLMalformedIsValidationError (break-out attempt, DROP TABLE attempt, dotted id). Proven non-vacuous — fails without the fix, passes with it. Full suite + vet green.

data.title: Core/CLI: serverless CLI — auto-select backend (direct core+sqlite vs HTTP)

fields.description:
Let read/write CLI commands work without a running HTTP server, in addition to (not instead of) the server.

Already partly true: the transport-agnostic core (internal/core) is shared by all surfaces, and export/import/mcp already skip HTTP — they call sqlite.Open + core.NewService directly against the workspace DB. Extending list/get/create/patch/... to do the same is mostly wiring.

Why: zero-config one-shots (`cards list` in a .cards/ dir just works, matching the new git-style workspace resolution); lower latency; no port/URL bookkeeping.

Two catches that mean HTTP cannot simply be dropped: (1) the event bus is in-process — a CLI writing directly to the DB bypasses a running server bus, so SSE live updates and status_changed hooks would not fire; (2) SQLite is single-writer across processes — direct writes while `cards serve` holds the DB risk SQLITE_BUSY/lock contention (WAL allows concurrent readers).

Clean design (matches ARCHITECTURE notes): CLI auto-selects its backend — if CARDS_URL is set or a server is detected, use HTTP so events/hooks/SSE stay correct; otherwise open core+sqlite directly for a fast serverless one-shot. Cost: a small backend interface the CLI commands target, with HTTP and direct-service implementations behind it.

work_log.author: jeremy
work_log.notes: Implemented via a cli.Transport seam: in-process backend runs the real /v1 router (httptest) against the resolved workspace; HTTP backend used when CARDS_URL set. No CARDS_URL => serverless. Reuses full handler/service stack, zero duplication. Tested + e2e verified.

Phase 5 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-11.md, first step — authored BEFORE the supervisor code so the load-bearing vocabulary is not rushed into the first PR. Startable early, during the P3 window: depends only on P2b. If the sprint compresses, cut P5 implementation scope before cutting this ADR.

a) RestartPolicy (on-failure/always/never + bounded backoff shape) reconciled with the existing Autostart bool — Autostart is the enable-gate, RestartPolicy the recovery shape.
b) RestartPolicy on kind:hook or kind:run is a load-time REJECTION per the P2b fail-loud rule, not a silent no-op.
c) The service-vs-run boundary stated: long-running-supervised vs one-shot.
d) The event-delivery boundary: services dial /v1/events/stream as ordinary API clients (per EXTENSIONS.md), making the one supervisor deliberately BIMODAL — hooks get in-process bus + subprocess-per-event; services get pure process lifecycle and NO event feeding. Recorded as an intentional decision so no later 'cleanup' unifies them.
e) The expose (Port/Protocol) field stays untouched — parsed but unconsumed; no reverse-proxy/port-registry door opens.

ACCEPTANCE: config.Extension gains a validated RestartPolicy (additive omitempty JSON) with load-time rejection of unknown values AND of the field on non-service kinds; the bimodal supervisor and SSE-client event boundary are recorded decisions in the ADR (docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md or new ADR file) + EXTENSIONS.md.

data.title: Sprint 07-22 P4: pin contracts (OpenAPI structural, error paths, SSE filters) + drive extension examples

fields.description:
Sprint 07-22 Phase 4 of docs/plans/2026-07-22-sprint-plan.md — pin the widest contract-bearing surfaces, then immediately spend them on runnable composition proof. Pin-then-demonstrate in one phase keeps the tests contract-weighted (they exist because the examples ride them), not coverage-vanity.

## Context
Depends on Phase 2 (the query endpoint the PR-sync example rides). The two example builds are EXISTING cards driven by this phase — fa6d5c2f (PR-sync) and 469c93e2 (changelog-from-cards); each carries a sprint-07-22 comment with the decided shape. This card owns the contract pins plus flipping the doc anchors.

## DO
1. **Pin apiOpenAPI structurally, not as a byte-golden** — a golden of openapi.Build() output pins the generator to itself and detects change, not correctness (and would ossify a latent handler bug). Property-based assertions instead: every card type appears, every documented field has a schema entry, error responses match the documented error envelope.
2. **Pin apiRelease and apiRemoveLink error paths** (version_conflict, not-found, invalid link type) by asserting against the structured-error shape documented in docs/spec — not current bytes.
3. **Cover SSE filtering behind documented query params** — filterBoardEvents (28.6% covered), cardInBoard (0%), cardOwnedBy (0%) — reusing the internal/httpapi/sse_test_hooks.go pattern with dialed-down keepalive; add NO new timing assumptions. Keep contract goldens in files decoupled from /ui template internals (mirror render_golden_test.go separately); skip boilerplate (uiAsset, uiStylesheet, SetVersion).
4. **Drive the two example cards to done** (469c93e2 first if time is tight is WRONG — see cut rule below): changelog-from-cards (469c93e2, type_id-grouped) and PR-sync (fa6d5c2f, GitHub-Action variant riding POST /v1/cards/query).
5. **Flip the doc-status anchors in the SAME change**: docs/using-cards.md 'Pull requests'/'Changelogs' → built, docs/extensions/index.md worked examples, implementation-status.md anchors; record the rollback note per the Phase-1 DoD rule.

## Cut rule (if the phase slips)
Contract tests land FIRST (they gate Phase 5). The changelog example is the cuttable tail; PR-sync stays — it is the composition proof the sprint is named for.

## Expected outcomes / exit
- A regression in OpenAPI generation or release/link error shapes fails a test that encodes the SPEC, not a self-referential golden.
- board_id and owner SSE filtering verified against docs/events/events-history.md deterministically.
- Both examples runnable (see their cards); docaudit tests (TestImplStatusAnchorsResolve, TestImplStatusBoundaryCommit) pass; no stale [proposed] claim remains.

## Demo
Run the PR-sync harness on a canned payload and watch the card move on the live board via the query endpoint; generate a changelog between two tags that reads cleanly on the mixed dogfood board.

data.title: TRACKER: Sprint 07-12 — honest ledger + SQLite concurrent-read spine

fields.description:
SPRINT TRACKER (parent) — not an implementation card. Do not implement work here; drive and close child cards. Executable detail lives on the children.

Plan of record (archived narrative snapshot):
  docs/archive/2026-07-sprints/sprint-2026-07-12.md
Note: docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-12.md is gone (moved to archive). Later sprint docs/plans/2026-07-18-sprint-plan.md already folded P1 hygiene + P2a landing into the 07-18 pass; this tracker remains the parent map for the original 07-12 child set until P2b/P3 finish or park.

## Why this sprint exists

Infra-only. No new board/CLI feature for end users. Two outcomes:

1. **Honest planning ledger** — docs and board cards match what the code already does, so agents stop re-implementing shipped work (and auth stays a frozen design, not code built here).
2. **Measured path to concurrent SQLite reads** — production today still uses one connection (`Open` → `MaxOpenConns(1)` + `_txlock=immediate` in `internal/sqlite/sqlite.go`). Multi-agent traffic can queue every read behind that single conn. Before changing production, measure on file-backed WAL through a real transport; only then ship a reader pool, a write-hold reduction, or park with evidence.

## Children (phase map)

| Phase | Short id | Role | Status (verified) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1a | 29200d8b | Ledger truth: date min/max shipped, coverage fix, behavior drift test | done |
| P1b | 7a3f4ebd | Auth closeout: ROADMAP §1 → frozen auth.md; park bearer impl | done |
| P1c | 8f8cbde7 | One canonical read-pool card (57e1bde9); ROADMAP §3 cites it | done |
| P2a | 77d6c663 | Shared-cache **test** harness (`internal/sqlite/sqlitetest`); migrate in-memory tests | done |
| P2b | 495d2e09 | Measured file-WAL read-under-write baseline + written a/b/c verdict | backlog (open) |
| P3 | 57e1bde9 | CANONICAL: reader pool **or** write-hold cut **or** park — scope set by P2b | backlog (open) |

### Standing rules
- P1 was parallel bookkeeping (not the spine) — complete.
- P2a was the test seam only; it does **not** replace production `MaxOpenConns(1)`. Code confirms production still single-conn; `OpenDSN` is the test-harness seam.
- P3 scope is **decided by P2b's measured verdict**, not assumed. Verdict (c) "park with evidence" is success.
- Measure only on **file-backed WAL** through HTTP/MCP (`:memory:` has no fsync and fakes the verdict).
- Keep pragma/DSN construction centralized if/when a second DSN appears (two DSNs = drift risk).

### Remaining spine (what is left)
1. Finish **495d2e09 (P2b)** — baseline + written a/b/c go/no-go on the canonical card.
2. Finish or park **57e1bde9 (P3)** per that verdict. Do not open pool code until the verdict exists.

## Out of scope (deliberate)
- AUTH reference implementation (350b1bac — own XL sprint; never stack with the pool)
- In-core authz / RBAC / sessions / multi-tenant (auth.md non-goals stand)
- Re-implementing date min/max (shipped; P1a was ledger correction only)
- Rewriting frozen auth.md
- Fake user-visible demo feature just to decorate an infra sprint
- Postgres / alt backends (deferred until WAL path is proven or parked)
- `/ui/definitions` read-only view (8903f9aa)
- Outbox/tailer webhooks (parked behind OUTBOX-GONOGO)

## Done when
- Every child above is `done` (or P3 explicitly closed as parked-with-evidence after P2b verdict c).
- Plan/archive path on this card stays accurate; no agent is sent to a missing `docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-12.md`.
- Production still matches the chosen outcome: pool landed with tests, write-hold reduced with tests, or single-conn retained with P2b evidence on 57e1bde9.
- Sprint close: export + commit workspace JSONL once after residual children close (do not edit JSONL by hand while a server is live on the same workspace).

## Verify (parent-level)
- `cards get` each child id in the table; statuses match the table or are newer-done.
- `test -f docs/archive/2026-07-sprints/sprint-2026-07-12.md`
- `rg -n 'SetMaxOpenConns|OpenDSN|sqlitetest' internal/sqlite/` — harness present; production `Open` still `openDSN(dsn, 1, ws)` until P3 lands a deliberate change.
- After P2b: verdict a/b/c written on 57e1bde9.
- After P3 (if a or b): concurrent-read or write-hold tests pass race-clean on file+WAL; measured numbers recorded.

data.title: UI: expand link chips to reveal target cards (hover/preview)

fields.description:
**Problem (validated):** on the board view, card links are shown only as COUNT stats — `card_partial.html:47-48` renders `{{.OutCount}}` / `{{.InCount}}` as bare numbers with `data-stat="out"`/`data-stat="in"`. (The card MODAL already shows full link titles — `card_modal.html:225-237`, `.rel` chips with `OutLinks`/`InLinks` — so this card is board-view-only.)

**Scope:** make the board's link count stats explorable without leaving the board.
1. Hover (or click/tap, for touch) a link count stat to reveal a small popover listing the target card titles, grouped by link type (depends-on / blocked-by / etc.), each clickable to open that card's modal.
2. Keyboard-accessible (focus → expand; Esc to dismiss).
3. Reuse the existing `LinkView`/`cardRelations` data (render.go:194, :358) — no new data path.

**Start simple (chip + hover), iterate.** Faint connector lines / graph view are explicitly LATER.

**Palette / visual language** is owned by the design-language card (fca1f3d5, depends-on); this card consumes that language, it does not invent one.

**Done when:** hovering/focusing a card's link count on the board shows the target card titles (not just a number) without a full page/modal navigation; the popover is keyboard-dismissable; targets link through to the existing card modal. No new dependency-graph rendering.

data.title: pi-cards: interactive board UI, SSE live refresh, /cards show, #id mentions (P2)

fields.description:
pi-cards series 5/8 — interactive board UI, SSE live refresh, /cards show, #id mentions (P2). Spec §6.1, §6.2. Blocked by card 4 (write surface).

All tools exist; this is the daily-driver surface. Full-screen board component in tui mode with the Go TUI's proven keymap, live refresh over SSE in HTTP mode, plus the context-injection features (`/cards use`, `#short-id` autocomplete, `cards-card` message renderer).

Scope:
- `src/board-ui.ts`: full-screen component via `ctx.ui.custom`; lanes as columns, cards as rows; keys `h/l/j/k` nav, `enter` scrollable detail (description, fields, links, comments, worklog; `esc` back), `/` filter, `s` status move (options = board's declared transitions for that card, from `GET /v1/boards/:id`), `o` owner, `m` claim/release to self, `c` comment via `ctx.ui.editor`, `n` new card (type picker → title → required-fields wizard), `e` schema-driven field edit (enum→select, date→input, text→editor), `w`/`g` stubs wired in cards 6/7, `?` help, `q` quit.
- HTTP mode: SSE `GET /v1/events/stream` with `Last-Event-ID` resume refreshes lanes; CLI mode shows "press `r` to refresh" and never claims liveness (§5.1).
- `src/context.ts`: `/cards use <id>` → `pi.sendMessage({customType:"cards-card", display:true, …})`; `pi.registerMessageRenderer("cards-card", …)` compact render (type badge, short-id, title, status/owner, description, acceptance, links); `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider` on `#` completing short-id+title; input transform expands bare `#<id>` to `[#<id> "<title>"]` (§6.2).

Implementation notes (verified against pi 0.80.10 types.d.ts + tui.md):
- Component contract: factory `(tui, theme, keybindings, done) => Component` where Component = `{ render(width): string[], handleInput?(data), invalidate(), dispose?() }`. Keyboard input arrives via `handleInput(data)`; match keys with `matchesKey(data, "escape")` from `@earendil-works/pi-tui` (there is no `onKey`). `done(value)` resolves the `ctx.ui.custom<T>` promise and closes the component.
- Full-screen (replacing the normal UI) is the default; overlay is opt-in via `{ overlay: true }` second arg — do not use overlay here.
- Call `tui.requestRender()` (or `invalidate()`) after state changes.
- No colors outside `theme.fg("accent"|"muted"|"dim", …)`.
- SSE runs only while the component is open; abort on the close path via AbortController.
- `ctx.ui.custom()` returns `undefined` in rpc mode → fall back to the card-3 text board; print/json modes unchanged.
- `w` (work) and `g` (export) keys render but notify "not yet implemented" — wired in cards 6/7.

Acceptance:
- `pi -e ./src/index.ts` (tui) → `/cards` opens the full-screen board; `j/k` moves selection, `enter` shows detail, `s` on a todo card offers only `in_progress` (engineering transitions), move succeeds and persists (`cards get <id>` shows new status).
- With `cards serve` running: create a card from a second terminal → board refreshes without restart (SSE); kill server, reconnect honors `Last-Event-ID`.
- Serverless CLI mode: hint text shown, `r` re-lists.
- `/cards use <id>` renders a `cards-card` message in the transcript; typing `#` offers short-id completions; submitting `#<id>` expands to `[#<id> "<title>"]` in the sent prompt.
- `node --test` + typecheck green.

Out of scope: `ctx.ui.setWidget` ambient board summary (spec open question #4 — defer); `cards_work` behind `w` (card 6); git export behind `g` (card 7).

fields.description:
## What shipped

The documentation now checks itself against the code. Every file-and-line reference in the implementation-status page is pinned to a real code symbol, so when a function moves or gets renamed, a test fails instead of the docs silently pointing at the wrong place. Ten stale references were fixed in the process. Contributors and agents can now trust that a documented location is a real one.

---

Phase 1 of docs/plans/2026-07-19-sprint-plan.md — foundation. Make the doc that enforces docs-vs-code honesty itself honest and machine-checked, with an extraction contract explicit enough that the guard cannot green-light the moved-and-renumbered rot class that recurred. No `internal/` kernel code changes.

## DO
1. **Roll the boundary.** `docs/reference/implementation-status.md` L619 ("Current boundary: `b3bfed5` → HEAD (`0421efd`, …)") → `bb6ffc5`. Split the temporal-breaches `1247e3b` evidence row into its own entry under the new boundary. Do NOT re-audit §4–§8 across the 17 new commits (scope discipline).
2. **Re-pin the 3 rotted anchors** (verified against HEAD `bb6ffc5`), each annotated with the explicit guard marker:
   - `internal/core/service.go:1491` — `claimWithRetry` call site
   - `internal/core/service.go:1526` — `func claimWithRetry`
   - `internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:730` — `return … ErrClaimRaced`

4. **Complete the CLAUDE.md "Where things live" table** — add the 7 missing `internal/` packages: `artifacts`, `cli`, `docaudit`, `openapi`, `seed`, `starter`, `themecss`.
5. **Add the guard** — `TestImplStatusAnchorsResolve` in `internal/docaudit/docaudit_test.go`. Extraction contract: each citation carries an explicit parseable HTML-comment marker `<!-- guard: <path>:<line>[-<end>] symbol=<ident> -->` (NOT prose regex). Add the boundary-commit assertion: cited commit exists in `git rev-list HEAD` and within N=20; on breach, fail with a message naming the one-line fix. The within-N check is a WARNING in normal `go test`, STRICT only in a dedicated docaudit CI job (`-tags=strictdoc`); anchor + doc-path tests strict everywhere.

- [ ] CLAUDE.md table lists all 14 `internal/` packages.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/docaudit ./internal/httpapi ./internal/config` green; `go vet ./...` clean.

`go test ./internal/docaudit/ -run TestImplStatusAnchorsResolve -v` PASS; `grep -rn "docs/SPEC.md\|docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\|docs/DEVELOPER-REFERENCE.md\|docs/MCP.md" internal/ cmd/` empty.

data.title: TRACKER: Sprint 07-19 — verifiable contracts self-checking + runnable extension seed

fields.description:
## What shipped (sprint summary)

This sprint made Cards more trustworthy and more extensible: the docs now verify themselves against the code, board snapshots are proven to round-trip exactly, a runnable example extension shows how to automate on top of Cards, and the terminal UI gained the web UI's filter and sort powers. Details live on the four child cards.

---

SPRINT TRACKER (parent) — not an implementation card. Drive and close the four phase children; executable detail lives on them and in the plan.
    
    Plan of record: docs/plans/2026-07-19-sprint-plan.md
    
    ## Why this sprint exists
    
    Make Cards' verifiable contracts self-checking and its extension model runnable, so contributors and agents land on real files, real lines, and a real running composition seam — not 404s, rotten anchors, or spec-only claims. Three of four phases buy trust (docs/code honesty, portable-state pinning, composition proof); one phase (P4) ships the only visible feature (TUI sort/filter parity). No kernel schema changes, no new dependencies, no new languages.
    
    ## Children (phase map)
    
    | Phase | Short id | Title | Effort | Kind | Status |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | P1 | cc469ca0 | SoT refresh + anchor guard (implementation-status.md → HEAD, symbol-pairing guard) | M | infra | todo |
    | P2 | 5628c87b | JSONL snapshot residual gaps (CLI wrapper, byte-stability, frozen fixture, board.sh smoke) | S | infra | todo |
    | P3 | db5b3383 | Runnable cards-extension seed (review-bot.mjs SSE→take-next→comment, automated test) | M | feature | todo |
    | P4 | e3103027 | TUI filter/sort parity (shared sortOptions, non-colliding keys, me-substitution test) | M | feature | todo |
    
    Thread: orient (P1) → pin (P2) → prove (P3) → parity (P4). P2/P3/P4 are independent after P1; ordering the composition climax (P3) before the polish capstone (P4) keeps the north-star's "runnable" prong front-loaded.
    
    ## Standing rules
    - No `internal/` kernel code changes in P1/P2. P3 adds only an example + extensions.json + docs. P4 touches `internal/tui` + a new shared render package (`internal/uioptions`), NOT `internal/core`.
    - The anchor guard's extraction contract is an explicit `<!-- guard: path:line symbol=... -->` marker, not prose regex. Negative proof #2 (symbol moved, line bumped to a different function) is a named exit criterion.
    - P2 fixture is frozen + hash-pinned (`cmd/cards/testdata/backlog.frozen.jsonl`); the live `.cards/backlog.jsonl` is NOT a test input.
    - P3 seeds a cards-extension `service`, NOT the pi-extension (philosophy §6 — pi-extension ships in its own repo). Temp workspace is provisioned from `examples/demo-workspace` (carries engineering board + the pre-existing `review-notify` hook on the same event — test asserts on the bot's author specifically).
    - P4 sort presets sourced from a shared `sortOptions` helper in `internal/uioptions` (compile-time parity, not review-time). `/` stays find; filter modal on `f`.
    
    ## Out of scope (deliberate)
    - `work_cards` / `@work-cards/client` convenience library (L+, new dep)
    - TUI link-follow navigation / cross-board jump (borderline L)
    - Rolling the SoT boundary §4–§8 re-audit across all 17 new commits

    - Board-inventory hygiene; release tag v0.1.4

data.title: Sprint 07-19 P3: Runnable cards-extension seed (review-bot.mjs SSE→take-next→comment, automated test)

fields.description:
## What shipped

Cards now ships a working example extension: a small review bot (one file, no dependencies) that listens to the board's live event stream, picks up cards that reach review, and leaves a comment on them. It reconnects cleanly if the server restarts, and an automated end-to-end test proves the whole loop. It's the template to copy when you want to build your own automation on top of Cards.

---

Phase 3 of docs/plans/2026-07-19-sprint-plan.md — composition climax. Demonstrate "extensions over plugins" (philosophy §6) with one real running process and an AUTOMATED test proving the SSE → take-next → comment loop. This is the sprint's central proof, not a manual demo.

> FRAMING (decisive): seed a runnable **cards-extension** `service`, NOT the pi-extension. `docs/design/pi-extension.md` §4 ships the pi extension in its own repo for four stated reasons; proceeding literally is a philosophy-§6 regression. The entire substrate already exists and is `[built]`: `--run-extensions` (`cmd/cards/serve.go:63`), supervisor handles `kind: service` with autostart/restart_policy/backoff (own tests), service processes get `CARDS_URL`/`CARDS_WORKSPACE`/`CARDS_USER` in env (`internal/hooks/services.go:177`), `POST /v1/cards/take-next` + `POST /v1/cards/{id}/comments` exist, SSE resumption via `Last-Event-ID`/`since=` is implemented. No `internal/` kernel changes.

## DO
1. **Seed the extension.** New file `examples/demo-workspace/.cards/ext/review-bot.mjs` — ~150 lines (reconnect-with-backoff, `Last-Event-ID` tracking, structured log push this past the naive ~80), Node stdlib `fetch` + hand-rolled SSE line reader (NO npm deps). Loop: subscribe to `/v1/events/stream` (send `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect) → on `status_changed → review` → `POST /v1/cards/take-next` → `POST /v1/cards/:id/comments`. Lift the snippet at `docs/events/integration.md:37-95`. On connect, log a stable `{"event":"subscribed","lastEventId":...}` JSON line (stable grep target for the stability test).
2. **Wire the supervisor declaration.** Add a `service` entry to `examples/demo-workspace/definitions/extensions.json` (`autostart: true`, `restart_policy: on-failure`, `run: ["node",".cards/ext/review-bot.mjs"]`). No `internal/hooks/` changes. Behind `--run-extensions` (not default-on).
3. **Doc-status fixes.** In `docs/extensions/index.md`: add "Example 7 — runnable SSE worker (Node service) `[built]`"; fix the stale `[built — external]` vs `[proposed]` mismatch on Example 6. In `docs/design/pi-extension.md`: clarify the one-line status. Cite `docs/events/integration.md:37` from the new example.
4. **Node runtime gate.** README states the Node requirement. Supervisor logs a clear `node: not found — service review-bot skipped` line on a Node-less machine, not a silent restart loop.
5. **Automated test (BLOCKER).** `scripts/review-bot_test.sh` (bash harness, runnable standalone AND via a `go test` wrapper so it lives in `go test ./...`):
   - build `cards`, start `cards serve --workspace <temp> --run-extensions` on a temp workspace **provisioned from `examples/demo-workspace`** (carries engineering board with `review` status + the bot's `extensions.json` declaration — temp workspace is a COPY of the demo workspace, not empty),
   - create a card, transition it to `review`,
   - assert the bot's comment appears via `cards show --json`, scoped to the **bot's** author identity (the demo workspace already ships a `review-notify` HOOK (`extensions.json` id `review-notify`, `on: status_changed`, filter `board_id: engineering, to_status: review`) firing on the identical event; two extensions on one transition is an intentional hook-vs-service illustration — assert on the bot's comment specifically, not "something happened"),
   - SSE resumption (MAJOR): kill/restart server mid-stream, drive a second card to `review`, assert bot resumes from last event id, no missed `status_changed`,
   - supervisor stability (MAJOR): assert bot reaches `subscribed` within N seconds (default 10, env-tunable `REVIEW_BOT_SUBSCRIBE_TIMEOUT` for loaded CI) and restarts ≤1× in a 5s window.
6. **No-npm-deps assertion.** Exit criterion greps the seed for `require(`/`import` from non-stdlib and asserts empty.

## ACCEPTANCE (binary)
- [ ] `review-bot.mjs` runs under supervisor with `--run-extensions`, zero npm deps (grep passes), sends `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect.
- [ ] `scripts/review-bot_test.sh` (BLOCKER) PASS: `status_changed → review` triggers a comment on the card, asserted via `cards show --json` scoped to the bot's author.
- [ ] SSE resumption test (MAJOR) PASS: kill/restart mid-stream; bot resumes from last event id, no missed event.
- [ ] Supervisor stability test (MAJOR) PASS: bot reaches `subscribed` within N (default 10, env-tunable); ≤1 restart in 5s window.
- [ ] `extensions.json` declares the `service` with autostart + restart policy.
- [ ] Node requirement in README; supervisor logs clear "node: not found — skipped" on Node-less machines.
- [ ] Doc-status tags fixed (Example 6 mismatch, Example 7 added, `pi-extension.md` one-liner).
- [ ] No `internal/` kernel code changed; `go build ./...` clean.

## DEMO
`scripts/review-bot_test.sh` PASS; `grep -nE 'require\(|import ' examples/demo-workspace/.cards/ext/review-bot.mjs | grep -v 'node:'` empty.

Parent/tracker: card_cf3ba12a. Example + extensions.json + docs + test; no kernel code.

data.title: Sprint 07-19 P4: TUI filter/sort parity (shared sortOptions, non-colliding keys, me-substitution test)

fields.description:
## What shipped

The terminal UI can now slice the board the same way the web UI does. Press `f` to filter (including "my cards"), `F` to cycle through sort presets, `T` to narrow by card type, and `/` still finds by text. The sort presets are literally shared code with the web UI, so the two interfaces can never drift apart. Screenshot attached below.

---

Phase 4 of docs/plans/2026-07-19-sprint-plan.md — user-value capstone (the sprint's only visible feature). Close the TUI/web parity gap so the TUI is a credible daily driver of the same query surface, with sort presets sourced from the web UI's `boardSortOptions` and `/` (find) kept distinct from the filter modal.

> RESCOPING: outbound links already render (since `0421efd`); `0d33bdd` fixed inbound links. This phase ships sort/filter parity ONLY; link-follow is out of scope.

## DO
1. **Wire the query surface into `refresh`.** `internal/tui/tui.go:438` (`refresh`) builds `core.CardQuery{BoardID, Limit:500, Include:["links","comments"]}` with no `Sort`/`Owner`/`TypeID`/`Filter`. Add model fields for active sort/owner/type/filter and compose them into the query. Do `me`→actor substitution for saved filters (actor is `m.actor`). Transport-conflation fix: the TUI is serverless/in-process (`tui.go:443` calls `m.svc.ListCards` directly) — there is no HTTP 422; bad sort/filter DSL returns a Go `*core.Error` from `ListCards` (`service.go` validates sort via `ParseSort` up front), surfaced via `notifyErr`.
2. **Non-colliding keybindings.** `/` stays Search (find) at `tui.go:217`. New bindings: `f` — filter modal (server-side jq-DSL; owner/type narrows live here too; NOT `/`); `F` — sort-cycle; `T` — type-filter. Owner-filter folded into `f` (no separate `O` binding — avoids the `o`/`O` muscle-memory trap). `s` (status) and `o` (edit-owner) untouched. Update `FullHelp` group 2: row reads `f filter / F sort / T type / / find`, with `s status` and `o owner` separate. Store active directives on the model so they survive a bus-driven `refresh` (which rebuilds the query from scratch).
3. **Source sort presets from `boardSortOptions` (compile-time parity).** "Parity" = TUI offers the same labeled presets the web UI ships (`internal/httpapi/ui.go:402` `boardSortOptions`: `-updated_at` "Recently updated", `-created_at` "Newest", `created_at` "Oldest", `title` "Title (A–Z)", plus board `LaneSort` "Board default") and respects `board.Presentation.LaneSort`. Extract a shared `sortOptions(active, board)` helper into a NEW small shared render package `internal/uioptions` — NOT `internal/core` (presentation label; core grows reluctantly per philosophy; the plan's earlier hedge is resolved away from core). `internal/httpapi/ui.go` calls the shared helper. TUI and web UI cannot drift.
4. **Tests.** `internal/tui/tui_test.go`: sort-order (set `m.sort = "-created_at"`, `m.refresh`, assert `m.cards[0].CreatedAt >= m.cards[len-1].CreatedAt`); `me`-substitution regression (set `m.filter = "owner == me"`, `m.refresh`, assert only `m.actor`'s cards return); filter-modal behavior assertion.
5. **Note the bus boundary.** Add a line to `docs/design/tui-bus-disposition.md` that filter/sort changes trigger a re-fetch (not a bus round-trip); cross-reference the surviving-directive test so the invariant is machine-checked.

## ACCEPTANCE (binary)
- [ ] `Sort`/`Owner`/`TypeID`/`Filter` wired into `refresh`; `me` substitution + DSL-error surfacing (`*core.Error` from `ListCards` via `notifyErr` — no HTTP 422).
- [ ] `/` (find) and `f` (filter modal) are separate bindings; `F` sort, `T` type; owner-filter folded into `f`; `s`/`o` untouched. `FullHelp` group 2 updated and reviewable.
- [ ] TUI sort options equal `boardSortOptions` output for the active board (MAJOR), via shared `sortOptions` helper in `internal/uioptions` (compile-time parity).
- [ ] Sort-cycle + filter-modal keys bound; directives survive `refresh`.
- [ ] `me`-substitution regression test (MAJOR) PASS: `m.filter = "owner == me"` returns only `m.actor`'s cards.
- [ ] Tests assert sort order + filter behavior; `go test ./internal/tui` green.
- [ ] `tui-bus-disposition.md` cross-references the surviving-directive test.
- [ ] No new deps; no schema/API churn; `go build ./...` clean.

## DEMO
`./cards --workspace ./examples/demo-workspace` (bare = TUI): `f` + "tag:bug" → filter modal; `F` → cycle sort to "Newest"; `/` still find; `go test ./internal/tui -run 'TestSort|TestFilter' -v` PASS.

data.title: Sprint 07-11 P3b: --watch definitions poller + definition_reload_failed in-browser banner + reload contract

fields.description:
Phase 3 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-11.md. Audience: the definition author with a BROWSER open — the philosophy's headline daily-DX win: edit git-backed JSON, see it live, including seeing it FAIL live. Decides the reload-contract seam ONCE so P5 inherits answers, not contradictions.

DO:
1) Optional --watch flag wiring a definitions/ watcher into reloadableApp.reloadLocked(). Dependency-free poller modeled on scripts/dev-server.sh's fingerprint-hash loop — NO fsnotify (principle 10). Designed for testability from the start: injectable clock + synchronously-drivable scan function so debounce/coalescing/self-write tests assert deterministically — no real sleeps, no -race flake.
2) Self-write suppression via a suppression token set by handleCreateBoard's write-then-reload path — NEVER sharing reloadableApp.mu with the poll loop, so the poller can never block the HTTP write path.
3) Failure channel decided NOW, in the author's favor: a broken JSON edit keeps the last-good generation serving AND emits definition_reload_failed on the bus; the UI (ui.go already listens for definition_reloaded) shows a banner/toast with the structured error. stderr is additive, not primary — under --watch there is no HTTP response to carry the error and the author is looking at the browser.
4) Write the reload-contract note covering: debounce policy, self-write suppression, supervisor-generation provenance (from P3a), failure surfacing, mutex serialization.

DEMO CAVEAT: the SSE stream filters on card_type_ids only — default_filter is NOT applied. Do not script a demo that assumes board-scoped SSE.

ACCEPTANCE: saving a definition reloads live without dropping SSE; a burst of editor saves (atomic unlink+create, save-all) coalesces to exactly one reload; handleCreateBoard's own write does not double-fire; broken edit shows an in-browser banner within the debounce window while the board keeps serving last-good; banner clears on next successful reload; contract note written; tests run deterministically via injected clock; no new dependency.

data.title: Sprint 07-11 P5c: reconcile-on-reload — service identity key + decision table; zero churn on board-create reload

fields.description:
Phase 5 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-11.md, final step — its own design + implementation, DESIGNED BEFORE CODING: config.Result.Extensions is rebuilt per generation while the supervisor lives outside the reloadable seam.

DEFINE:
1) Service identity key: the extension ID; a change to command/args/env hashes as 'same service, changed declaration'.
2) Decision table: added = start; removed = drain+stop; unchanged = leave alone; declaration-changed = drain+restart.
3) Concurrency model: the reload swap holds reloadableApp.mu; the supervisor reconciles from a snapshot handed off AFTER the swap completes — never acquiring mu from the supervise loop, so no HTTP-handler deadlock.

TESTS: board-creation reload leaves running services untouched (zero churn); edited declaration restarts exactly that service; removed declaration stops it.

CLOSE-OUT: flip INTEGRATOR-REFERENCE.md section 7 (service kind) to [built] with the audit changelog updated.

ACCEPTANCE: routine board-create reload churns zero services; genuine declaration changes handled per the documented table; INTEGRATOR-REFERENCE section 7 flipped to [built]; go test ./... green and race-clean.

data.title: Events: condition events + monitors (WIP, time-in-status, empty lane, idle)

fields.description: Declarative board 'monitors' -> condition events on the bus. Instant (eval synchronously after the triggering mutation): wip_exceeded/cleared, lane_drained/refilled, card_blocked/unblocked. Temporal (status_timeout, card_idle): emitted by a monitor-evaluator goroutine beside the hook supervisor, driven by a deadline min-heap (sleeps until the earliest deadline, NO fixed tick; empty heap = no wakeups). Deadlines armed from a denormalized status_since column + a fired-marker keyed by (card,status,status_since); reconstructible from state, nothing persisted. Lazy/refcounted: deadlines scheduled only while a monitor has a live consumer (SSE filter, hook/webhook, or persist:true), dropped when the last consumer disconnects. Idempotent crossing-state tracking; core emits only, never acts. See docs/INTEGRATION.md.

PLAIN: today the core both declares transition rules (data) and enforces them (code). This RFC sketches moving enforcement behind a Validator interface with a subprocess callback seam, so policy richness lives at the boundary instead of growing an in-process rules dialect in core.

Planted for NEXT sprint. First-pass sketch for docs/design/BOARD-BEHAVIOR.md (does not yet exist). GOVERNING DOCS (frozen 2026-07-10, see docs/NOTES.md freeze entry): docs/design/CORE-BOUNDARIES.md §3.3 (three-layer framing + force policy) and docs/design/AUTH.md §7 (identity invariant). OUT of sprint 07-10 (see sprint tracker card_3f225267).

THREE-LAYER FRAMING (from CORE-BOUNDARIES §3.3 — adopt in the RFC):
- DECLARATIVE GRAPH (Board.Transitions in board JSON) = core DATA, introspectable/exportable — STAYS. Same family as columns and WIP limits.
- ENFORCEMENT (service.go:768, :1487 refusal) = the seam this RFC refactors behind a Validator interface, with in-core evaluate as the builtin first chain link.
- OBSERVATION (transition_rejected, events.go:282 TransitionRejectedDiff; constructed :291; emitted service.go:775) = stays wherever enforcement lives; continuity guaranteed.
The vision quote ('core should not have strong opinions about transitions') bans PROGRAMMABLE rules in core, not the declarative map.

OVERLAY PRINCIPLE at top of the doc:
'Core ships contracts and boring defaults. Policy richness lives at the boundary (auth adapter, validate callback, external hooks) — never as a growing in-process product dialect.'

SHAPE — data + code:
- Declared RULES (data): today's transitions: map, plus optional require_field_before etc. — read by a default builtin validator.
- Optional per-board VALIDATOR (subprocess declared in board JSON) returning a narrow verdict.
- Default = current EnforceTransitions behavior refactored behind the interface, so nothing regresses.

RUNTIME, DECIDED: SUBPROCESS-FIRST, single implementation. Embedded JS is EXPLICIT NON-GOAL until someone shows a demo subprocess can't carry. No behavior.js implicit paths — the board JSON declares a command.

BOARD DECLARATION (example):
  "behavior": { "validate": { "command": ["./extensions/eng-validate"], "timeout_ms": 200 } }

VERDICT WIRE SHAPE (JSON stdout of the subprocess):
  { "allow": true, "code": "transition_illegal", "message": "...",
    "field": "status", "valid_options": ["review"] }
Reuses existing structured-error vocabulary; no partial card mutations; no nested Service calls; max stdout size (documented).

FAIL-CLOSED MATRIX (writes only; reads never call this):
- timeout → fail-closed
- non-zero exit or unparseable JSON → fail-closed
- allow:false without a code → default transition_illegal (transitions) / validation_error (field triggers)
- subprocess missing / not executable → fail-closed with a CLEAR OPERATOR MESSAGE (config error, not a validation event)

CONTINUITY OF OBSERVATION: builtin deny and callback deny share the existing transition_rejected event/code path (events.go:282 already defines this today; emitted at service.go:775). Add an optional diff.source = "builtin" | "board_validate" only if it earns its keep in debugging — no new public event surface in v1.

EVENT COVERAGE, PHASED (avoids the workflow-engine siren):
- v1: status transitions only (patch/create status) — replaces in-core enforce.
- v1.1: declarative require_field_before_transition — ONE PATTERN ONLY ('status S requires field F set'), not a rules language. Compiles to the same Validator interface as the default builtin, so board subprocesses sit as chain peers, not special cases.
- v2: on_comment_added / on_field_changed validators ONLY IF real demand.

CHAIN ORDER: builtin declarative rules → board callback → commit. The callback does not reimplement column membership unless the operator opts into 'disable builtin.'

FORCE POLICY (decided 2026-07-10, CORE-BOUNDARIES §3.3 revised — this card is its durable home):
- Force is a PER-WRITE request field (force:true in PATCH body / req.Force / CLI --force), not a serve mode.
- force=true SKIPS BOTH the builtin declarative rules AND the board-callback validator — matches today's req.Force behavior (service.go:768); the web UI's drag-and-force-confirm flow depends on it. YOLO escape hatch by default.
- Force NEVER skips identity verification: under --auth token/proxy an unauthenticated forced write is 401 (AUTH.md §7). Attribution of a forced write is the resolved verified identity.
- NO NEW EVENT TYPE: forced-ness rides status_changed with diff.forced=true. A separate transition_forced EventType was considered and rejected (SPEC + bus-filter + INTEGRATOR churn without consumer demand).
- BOARD OPT-OUT: settings.allow_force:false makes the declarative graph a hard floor for that board (no force override there). Data, not code — same family as enforce_transitions. Small SPEC-DATA-MODEL addition.

HOOKS / VALIDATORS COVENANT (the load-bearing distinction — PHILOSOPHY §5 boundary):

| Seam                | Timing                      | Power                    | Contract |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------------|----------|
| Hooks (today)       | post-commit, at-most-once   | observe / side effects   | no veto |
| Validators (proposed)| pre-commit, sync, bounded  | verdict only             | no email/HTTP/card writes from the sandbox; if a validator does that via its own subprocess, that's the operator's problem — core provides no client helpers |

MIGRATION STORY: boards with today's enforce_transitions: true and no custom behavior → IDENTICAL outcomes; transition_rejected event still fires; no observable regression.

OPEN TENSIONS (decided next sprint, not now):
- Validator sync cost on every write: queue depth, panic isolation, dry-run escape hatch.
- Definition-trust ≠ card-ACL: see AUTH.md implementation notes.

data.title: Tags: management tooling (CLI/UI) + propose flow + tag_policy UX

fields.description:
P1 — fixes the 'tag_set too small to categorize workstreams' pain.

**Current state (verified):** tags are a closed set defined in `workspace.json` (`tag_set`); the `tags` field validates against it. `tag_policy` defaults to `propose` (config.go:121), and under `propose` an unknown tag is a HARD reject with a hint (errors.go:57) — there is no proposal/accept path. There is NO `cards tags` CLI subcommand (only list/get/create/patch/.../workspace exist). The dev workspace is already `tag_policy: open` (workspace.json:64), so the earlier 'flip to open' unblock is DONE and removed from scope.

**Scope (this card):**
1. CLI: `cards tags add|list|remove|propose` (and `cards tags set <id> ...` for full replace) so the tag set is manageable without hand-editing workspace.json.
2. UI tag manager in workspace settings (list/add/remove tags; shows policy).
3. Propose flow: when `tag_policy=propose`, an unknown tag creates a pending proposal an admin can accept in one click (CLI + UI), rather than the current hard reject. Accepted proposals add the tag to `tag_set` and re-validate.
4. Document grouped/namespaced tags (`area:ui`, `prio:high`) as a convention in `docs/reference/workspace-and-boards.md` (or wherever tag_set is documented).

**Out of scope:** changing the default policy, multi-tenant tag isolation, or a tag-merge/rename operation.

**Done when:** an admin can add a tag from the CLI and the UI without editing JSON; an unknown tag under `propose` produces an accept/reject proposal instead of a bare reject; the namespacing convention is documented with examples. Core + CLI + UI.

data.title: Reconsider RemoveEntry CAS: HTTP DELETE passes version=0, skipping concurrency guard

fields.description: Service.RemoveEntry treats version==0 as 'no CAS' (skip the version check), and the HTTP DELETE handler passes 0 unconditionally. So concurrent entry deletes can clobber each other without a 409. Either: (a) require version on DELETE and return 409 on stale, or (b) document that entry deletes are last-writer-wins by design. Decide and implement/test accordingly.

work_log.author: pi
work_log.notes: Fixed: HTTP DELETE now requires ?version=N for CAS (was passing 0, skipping the concurrency check). Service rejects version=0 with validation_failed. Stale version yields 409. Tests: TestRemoveEntry_RequiresVersion (service + HTTP).

comments.author: foz
comments.body: Verified. Service.RemoveEntry: `if version != 0 && version != current.Version` — version==0 skips CAS. apiRemoveEntry passes version=0 unconditionally (no version in DELETE body). So concurrent entry deletes never 409. Decide: require version on DELETE (safer) or document last-writer-wins.

data.title: Extension example: PR sync - move linked card on merge

fields.description:
Shippable example extension: watch GitHub (a webhook service or a GitHub Action running the CLI) and patch the linked card to done when its PR merges; optionally comment on the PR when the card reaches review.

Today nothing moves a card automatically when a PR merges (docs/using-cards.md 'Pull requests'); this extension closes that loop and demonstrates the extension model end to end — an external process reacting to GitHub via the HTTP API + event stream. Companion to the existing review-notify demo hook (examples/demo-workspace/definitions/extensions.json).

SCOPE: a self-contained example under examples/ (or a sibling repo) with: a webhook receiver or Action workflow that listens for PR 'closed/merged' events; resolution of the PR's linked card (by branch, PR-title convention, or a field); a cards patch moving the card to done on merge; optionally a PR comment when the linked card reaches review (via the event stream). Documented in docs/using-cards.md 'Pull requests'.

OUT OF SCOPE: a generic GitHub integration framework; bi-directional sync of every field; auth/secret management beyond a documented env var.

DONE WHEN: merging a PR whose branch carries a linked card moves that card to done in the dogfooding board; the example ships with a README and runs against a test repo; docs/using-cards.md 'Pull requests' references it.

VERIFY: end-to-end — merge a PR linked to a backlog card; observe the card move to done via the extension.

data.title: pi-cards: CardsClient with HTTP + CLI backends, resolve chains, unit tests

fields.description:
pi-cards series 2/8 — CardsClient with HTTP + CLI backends. Spec §5.1, §5.2, §5.4, §5.5, §8. Blocked by card 1 (scaffold).

Scaffold exists; this is the foundation everything else consumes. Implement the `CardsClient` interface covering exactly the operations the tools need, with two swappable backends: HTTP (`fetch` against `/v1`) and serverless CLI (spawn `cards` per op). Backend selection, workspace resolution, and actor resolution land here so later cards never re-derive them.

Scope:
- `src/client.ts`: `CardsClient` interface — `workspace()`, `listCards(filter)`, `getCard(id)` (short-id last-8 alias), `searchCards(q)`, `createCard`, `updateCard` (version + one conflict retry per §5.5), `addComment`, `appendEntry`, `claim`, `release`, `takeNext`, `exportState(outPath)`. Parsed JSON in/out; errors carry the structured cards error body verbatim (incl. `valid_options`).
- `src/backend-http.ts`: base URL from config `url`/`CARDS_URL`/probe `http://127.0.0.1:8787`; `X-Work-Cards-Actor` header; `Idempotency-Key` uuid per logical op, reused on retry; workspace-id mismatch check via `GET /v1/workspace` = loud error (§5.2).
- `src/backend-cli.ts`: one spawn per op (`execFile("cards", [...,"--json"])`), actor via `--as`; map ops to CLI verbs (list/get/create/patch/claim/take-next/append/comment add/users register/export).
- `src/resolve.ts`: workspace chain §5.2 (setting → `CARDS_WORKSPACE` → walk up from `ctx.cwd` for `.cards/` → `$CARDS_HOME`/`~/.cards`) and actor chain §5.4 (setting → `CARDS_USER` → `USER` → `default_user`, `actorSuffix` applied).
- Unit tests per spec §8: HTTP backend against a node `http` mock with canned `/v1` responses; CLI backend against a fake `cards` shim on PATH.

Implementation notes:
- Known CLI gap: there is **no** `cards release` command (api-surface §13); map CLI release to `cards patch <id> --version N --owner ""` with a test asserting that against the real binary — if it fails, throw a structured "release requires HTTP backend" error instead.
- Retry helper: on `version_conflict` re-GET, re-apply delta, retry once; second conflict throws verbatim (§5.5).
- No SSE here (card 5); no tool registration (cards 3-4).

Acceptance:
- `node --test test/client.test.ts` passes: conflict-retry, idempotency-key reuse across retries, short-id resolution, structured-error passthrough, workspace-mismatch error.
- `node --test test/client.integration.test.ts` drives the real `cards` binary serverless against the fixture workspace through list/get/create/patch/claim/take-next.
- `npm run typecheck` green.

Out of scope: `pi.registerTool` wrappers (cards 3-4); SSE streaming and `/v1/events` catch-up feed; `/cards connect` status reporting.

TWO SPEC-RELEVANT DISCOVERIES: (1) short-id is LEADING-8 hex prefix of the id hex part (core.ResolveCard service.go:602), not last-8 as spec §6.3/card said — integration test falsified last-8 then pinned leading-8; (2) CLI release mapping patch --owner "" FALSIFIED (empty owner = no-op) — release() throws unsupported_backend naming POST /v1/cards/:id/release instead.
